requirement: Any numeric limit, frequency or range stated in the Annex is a floor, not a target; site values may be tighter but never looser.
system_implications: Master-data configuration of EM limits, particle limits, time windows and test frequencies must be validated against a locked Annex 1 minimum table; saving a looser value is blocked or needs a QA-approved documented justification.
verification_test: Try to configure a Grade A settle-plate action limit above the Annex 1 value; confirm the system rejects it or forces a QA justification record.

requirement: If a site applies Annex 1 principles to non-sterile or low-bioburden products it should record which principles are applied and show compliance with them.
system_implications: Product master should carry a flag 'Annex 1 principles applied (non-sterile)' with a list of the applied principles so the edition can be reused for low-bioburden intermediates without implying sterility claims.
verification_test: Create a non-sterile product with the flag; confirm the applied-principles list is mandatory and printed on the batch record header.

requirement: Starting and packaging materials need adequate control and testing so their bioburden and endotoxin/pyrogen levels suit use.
system_implications: Dispensing/issue step must check the material lot is QC-released and, where the specification includes bioburden or endotoxin, that those results are within limits before the lot can be consumed in the batch.
verification_test: Attempt to dispense a component lot whose endotoxin result is pending; confirm a hard stop.

requirement: A site-wide Contamination Control Strategy (CCS) defines the critical control points and the controls and monitoring that manage contamination risk; it is reviewed and updated actively.
system_implications: Master batch record steps that are CCS critical control points must be tagged with the CCS reference/version; the batch record header shows the CCS version in force at execution.
verification_test: Open an executed batch; verify every CCP-tagged step shows the CCS document ID and version that was effective on the execution date.

requirement: The CCS covers vendor approval (component sterilisation, single-use systems, critical service providers) and the transfer of critical information with outsourced parties such as contract sterilisers.
system_implications: When a component or SUS is sterilised by a contractor, the batch record must capture the contractor, the approved-vendor status and the sterilisation certificate/lot data received, and block use if the supplier is not approved.
verification_test: Issue a gamma-irradiated SUS lot from an unapproved vendor; confirm the step blocks; with an approved vendor confirm certificate ID is mandatory.

requirement: Changes to systems are assessed for their effect on the CCS both before and after they are implemented.
system_implications: Change control for master batch records, recipes and limits must include a mandatory CCS-impact field and a post-implementation effectiveness check before the change is closed.
verification_test: Submit a master record change without CCS impact assessment; confirm approval cannot be completed.

requirement: Monitoring or testing alone does not prove sterility; sterility should not rest solely on a terminal process or a finished-product test.
system_implications: Release workflow must not allow disposition based only on a passing sterility test; the review-by-exception checklist must require evidence that process, EM, utilities and sterilisation records were reviewed.
verification_test: Attempt QP certification with only a sterility result attached and process/EM review items open; confirm the system blocks it.

requirement: Finishing, storage and transport should not compromise the sterile product; container integrity, contamination and degradation risks and the registered storage conditions are to be considered.
system_implications: Post-fill steps (capping, inspection, labelling, storage, shipping) must record storage location and condition data and flag any excursion from registered storage conditions against the batch.
verification_test: Inject a cold-room temperature excursion for the location holding a batch; confirm a deviation link appears on the batch and blocks release until assessed.

requirement: Persons certifying or releasing sterile product need appropriate access to manufacturing and quality information and knowledge of sterile manufacture and its critical quality attributes.
system_implications: QP/QA role must have read access to the complete batch dossier (execution data, EM/PM, utilities, sterilisation, filter tests, APS status, deviations, lab results) from one screen; role assignment should check the user's sterile-manufacturing qualification.
verification_test: Log in as QP; confirm every linked data source is reachable from the batch; confirm a QP without the sterile-products training record cannot be assigned as certifier.

requirement: Every non-conformity (e.g. sterility failure, EM excursion, procedural deviation) is investigated before the batch is certified; the investigation assesses process/product impact and other potentially affected batches, and records why batches were included or excluded.
system_implications: Certification is hard-blocked while any linked deviation/investigation is open; each investigation must carry an impact-scope list of batches with a mandatory inclusion/exclusion rationale per batch, and the scope must be propagated to all listed batches.
verification_test: Link an EM excursion to batch A and list batch B as excluded without rationale; confirm closure is refused; confirm batch A certification is blocked until closure.

requirement: Root cause analysis of procedural, process or equipment failures should correctly identify product risk so CAPA is appropriate; risk decisions and residual-risk acceptance are documented with rationale.
system_implications: Deviation records raised from the eBMR must include root cause category, product-risk statement, CAPA link and residual-risk acceptance rationale fields before closure.
verification_test: Try to close a deviation raised in execution without root cause and CAPA; confirm refusal.

requirement: Component preparation, product preparation and filling are kept technically and operationally separated to prevent mix-ups and contamination.
system_implications: Each master record step must be bound to a named room/zone; the system checks the operator's scanned location matches the step's designated area and prevents concurrent use of a room by two incompatible activities or batches.
verification_test: Start component washing and compounding of another batch in the same room simultaneously; confirm a conflict warning/block.

requirement: RABS or isolators should be considered in the CCS for aseptic operations; any alternative (open) approach needs justification.
system_implications: Line/equipment master data must record the barrier technology (isolator open/closed, RABS open/closed, conventional) and, for conventional lines, a reference to the CCS justification; this drives which building blocks (glove tests, bio-decontamination, door-opening logs) are mandatory.
verification_test: Configure a conventional (no barrier) aseptic line without a CCS justification reference; confirm the line cannot be released for use.

requirement: Four cleanroom grades apply: A for high-risk critical-zone operations (filling, stopper bowl, open primary packs, aseptic connections under first air); B as background to A for aseptic work (unless isolator); C and D for less critical stages, isolator background, and preparation/filling of terminally sterilised products. Direct operator interventions in Grade A should be minimised.
system_implications: Every processing step carries a required grade; before step start the system verifies the room/zone classification status is current and its grade meets the requirement; steps involving exposed sterile product or aseptic connections must be Grade A.
verification_test: Assign an aseptic connection step to a Grade C room; confirm master record validation rejects it; expire the room qualification and confirm step start is blocked.

requirement: For aseptic preparation and filling, pressure differences of the Grade B background room are monitored continuously.
system_implications: The eBMR must pull the continuous differential-pressure trend for the Grade B background for the full processing window into the batch record and flag any time below limit.
verification_test: Replay BMS data with a 3-minute drop below set limit during filling; confirm the batch record shows the excursion and requires assessment.

requirement: Transfers into Grade A/B follow a one-way route, preferably sterilising items through a double-ended autoclave or depyrogenation oven/tunnel; otherwise a validated equivalent (transfer disinfection, RTP for isolators, bacteria-retentive filter for gases/liquids). Removal of items (materials, waste, EM samples) uses a separate one-way route or procedural time separation.
system_implications: Material transfer step records the item, the transfer method (double-door steriliser load ID / tunnel run / disinfection wipe-down with agent and contact time / RTP port / filter), and the validated transfer procedure ID; exit movements are recorded separately with time so time-based separation can be verified.
verification_test: Record an item entering Grade B by wipe-down; confirm agent lot, contact time and transfer SOP are mandatory; confirm an exit movement at an overlapping time triggers a separation warning where the line uses time-based separation.

requirement: Only items on an approved list, assessed in transfer validation, may enter Grade A/B through airlocks or hatches; items destined for Grade A are protected while crossing Grade B; any unlisted item needs prior exceptional approval with a recorded risk assessment and a QA-approved disinfection and monitoring plan.
system_implications: Transfer scanning checks each item against the approved transfer list; an unlisted item is blocked unless a pre-approved QA exception record (risk assessment + disinfection + extra monitoring) is linked; the exception is carried to batch review.
verification_test: Scan an unlisted tool at the Grade B pass-through; confirm block; link a QA-approved exception and confirm it proceeds and appears in the review-by-exception report.

requirement: Items moving from lower-grade or unclassified areas to higher-grade areas are cleaned and disinfected in proportion to risk and per the CCS.
system_implications: Transfer steps from lower to higher grades require a disinfection record (agent, lot, expiry, contact time, operator) before the item can be accepted in the higher grade.
verification_test: Attempt to accept an item into Grade C without a completed disinfection entry; confirm block; enter an expired disinfectant lot and confirm rejection.

requirement: Airlock and pass-through doors should not open simultaneously; A/B airlocks use interlocks, C/D airlocks at least visual/audible warnings; a time delay between interlocked doors may be set.
system_implications: Interlock bypass or simultaneous-open events captured by the BMS for rooms used by the batch should be imported into the batch timeline and require assessment when they fall inside the processing window.
verification_test: Feed an interlock-override event for the Grade B airlock during filling; confirm it appears on the batch exception list.

requirement: Cleanrooms keep positive pressure/airflow relative to lower grades in all operating states; adjacent rooms of different grades should differ by at least 10 Pa (guidance value); containment designs may differ, but air flowing into a critical zone should come from an equal or higher grade.
system_implications: Room-pair differential-pressure set points and alarm limits are master data with a 10 Pa minimum default between different grades; containment (negative-pressure) products require an explicit configuration with CCS reference.
verification_test: Configure a Grade B/C pair with an 8 Pa low limit; confirm a justification is demanded.

requirement: Airflow visualisation (smoke) studies at rest and in operation, including simulated interventions, demonstrate no ingress from lower to higher grades; videos are retained and results feed the EM programme.
system_implications: Line qualification status should include a current airflow-visualisation study reference; interventions defined in the master record should reference the smoke study that covered them, so a new intervention type is flagged as not yet visualised.
verification_test: Add a new corrective intervention to the intervention catalogue without a smoke-study reference; confirm it is flagged as unqualified.

requirement: Critical pressure differentials are continuously monitored and recorded with an instant alarm for air-supply failure or DP below limit; alarms may not be overridden without assessment; a response procedure exists; alarm delays are justified in the CCS; non-critical DPs are recorded at regular intervals.
system_implications: eBMR links to the BMS/EMS for each room used, stores the DP trend for the batch window, lists every alarm with acknowledgement user, time and assessment, and forces an impact assessment for any critical-DP alarm during open processing; manual DP readings for non-critical pairs are captured as recurring checks.
verification_test: Simulate a critical-DP alarm acknowledged with no assessment; confirm the batch cannot proceed to review until an assessment is entered.

requirement: Isolators and RABS separate Grade A from the surrounding room; item entry/removal risks during processing are minimised using high-capability transfer technologies; open isolators and RABS give first-air protection with unidirectional flow over exposed product; closed isolators may be turbulent only for simple operations; negative-pressure isolators only where containment is essential.
system_implications: Transfers into running isolators/RABS must be recorded by transfer technology (RTP alpha/beta port, mousehole, transfer isolator) with the validated method; negative-pressure isolator use must be flagged as a containment product configuration.
verification_test: Record an RTP transfer during an isolator run; confirm port ID, beta-container sterilisation reference and time are mandatory.

requirement: Minimum background grade: open isolator generally Grade C, closed isolator Grade D (decided by CCS risk assessment covering bio-decontamination, automation, glove manipulations, glove/barrier breach, transfers, door-open set-up); RABS for aseptic processing at least Grade B with airflow studies during interventions and door openings.
system_implications: Line master data holds the required background grade by technology; batch start verifies the background room's current classification meets it; RABS door openings are logged as events that need assessment.
verification_test: Assign a RABS line to a Grade C background room; confirm configuration is rejected.

requirement: Glove material suitability is demonstrated and the glove replacement frequency is defined in the CCS.
system_implications: Each glove/sleeve position has an installed date and a CCS-defined replacement interval; the system blocks batch start if any glove on the line is past its replacement date.
verification_test: Set a glove install date older than the replacement interval; confirm line start is blocked.

requirement: Isolator glove leak testing uses a suitable method at defined intervals, generally at minimum when each batch or campaign starts and when it ends (more often if campaign length requires); gloves are visually inspected at each use and after any manipulation that may affect integrity; for small manual batches the session start/end may be used.
system_implications: Master record inserts mandatory glove integrity test steps (per port: tester ID, result, pass/fail) before first aseptic operation and after the last; visual checks are prompted with each glove use; a failed end-of-batch test automatically raises a batch impact assessment covering the period since the last passing test.
verification_test: Enter a failed end-of-batch glove test on port 3; confirm a deviation is raised automatically and the affected time window (since last pass) is listed for impact assessment.

requirement: Integrity/leak testing of the isolator enclosure is performed at defined intervals.
system_implications: Line readiness check verifies the isolator leak test is within its defined interval before batch start.
verification_test: Expire the isolator leak-test due date; confirm batch start is blocked.

requirement: RABS Grade A gloves are sterilised before fitting and sterilised or bio-decontaminated by a validated method before each campaign; if exposed to the background during operation they are disinfected by an approved method after each exposure; they are visually checked at each use and integrity-tested periodically.
system_implications: RABS batch set-up requires glove sterilisation/bio-decontamination record for the campaign; each door opening/exposure event requires a glove disinfection entry; periodic glove integrity test status is checked at line start.
verification_test: Log a RABS door opening with glove exposure and omit disinfection; confirm the next aseptic step is blocked.

requirement: Cleaning and bio-decontamination of barrier systems are defined and controlled; cleaning comes before bio-decontamination (declared essential, see AN1-198); agents should be shown not to harm the product. Isolator interior bio-decontamination is automated, validated, run within defined cycle parameters with a sporicidal agent in gaseous/vapour form, with gloves extended and fingers separated.
system_implications: Isolator set-up requires, in order: cleaning record, then an automated bio-decontamination cycle record (cycle ID, recipe/version, agent lot, key parameters vs validated ranges, pass/fail, glove-extension confirmation); the aseptic phase cannot open unless the cycle passed and cleaning preceded it.
verification_test: Import a VHP cycle record with a parameter outside range; confirm aseptic set-up is blocked; record cleaning after the cycle and confirm the sequence error is flagged.

requirement: RABS interiors receive routine sporicidal disinfection by a validated method covering all interior surfaces.
system_implications: RABS preparation step records sporicidal agent, lot, expiry, method/SOP version and operator; due-date logic enforces the routine frequency.
verification_test: Skip the sporicidal step beyond its defined frequency; confirm line start is blocked.

requirement: Cleanrooms and clean-air devices (UDAF, RABS, isolators) are qualified per Annex 15 for at-rest and operational states; qualification/classification is kept distinct from routine EM.
system_implications: Room/device master records hold qualification status and expiry separately from EM results; eBMR checks qualification status at step start and does not treat routine EM data as qualification evidence.
verification_test: Set a UDAF qualification to expired; confirm steps bound to it cannot start even if recent EM is compliant.

requirement: Classification is scheduled so it does not affect product; initial classification in simulated operations; reclassification in simulated operations or during an APS.
system_implications: Scheduling module should prevent planning classification sampling inside a commercial batch processing window; allow tagging an APS batch as also serving for reclassification.
verification_test: Schedule classification sampling over a live commercial fill; confirm a conflict warning.

name: Cleanroom classification - max total particles per m3 (Table 1)
values: Grade A: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 3520; >=5um not specified (consider if CCS or trends indicate). Grade B: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 352000; >=5um at rest not specified / in operation 2930. Grade C: >=0.5um at rest 352000 / in operation 3520000; >=5um at rest 2930 / in operation 29300. Grade D: >=0.5um at rest 3520000 / in operation not predetermined (site sets from risk assessment and data); >=5um at rest 29300 / in operation not predetermined.

name: Microbial limits during cleanroom qualification (Table 2)
values: Grade A: no growth (air, settle, contact). Grade B: air 10 CFU/m3; settle plate 90mm 5 CFU/4h; contact 55mm 5 CFU/plate. Grade C: air 100; settle 50; contact 25. Grade D: air 200; settle 100; contact 50. Settle plates exposed for the operation and changed after max 4 h (exposure based on recovery studies, no desiccation). All tabulated methods used for a grade unless justified; non-CFU methods need scientifically justified, CFU-correlated limits.

name: Airflow, pressure and clean-up guidance values
values: Differential pressure between adjacent rooms of different grades: >=10 Pa (guidance). UDAF air speed at working position: 0.36-0.54 m/s homogeneous (guidance; other values only if justified in CCS). Clean-up period to return to at-rest particle limits after operations/line clearance: < 20 min (guidance, set in qualification). Settle plate max exposure 4 h per plate.

name: Cleanroom and clean-air equipment requalification maximum intervals
values: Grade A and B areas: max 6 months. Grade C and D areas: max 12 months. Minimum requalification content: total particle classification, final filter integrity, airflow volume, room DP verification, air velocity (risk-based for B/C/D but required for UDAF filling zones e.g. terminally sterilised filling, Grade A background and RABS; recovery test replaces velocity for non-UDAF). Also requalify after remedial action or significant change (air interruption, HVAC/design change, final filter change).

requirement: Grade A/B classification should include extra locations at critical points (point of fill, closure feeder bowls) chosen by documented risk assessment; at-rest limits should be regained after operations and line clearance within a clean-up period set in qualification (guidance under 20 minutes), which procedures should respect when cleanliness is disrupted.
system_implications: After line clearance/cleaning or a disruption, the eBMR starts a clean-up timer using the room's qualified clean-up period and prevents the next batch or resumption of aseptic activity until it has elapsed (and, where linked, until particle counts have returned to at-rest limits).
verification_test: Complete line clearance and immediately try to start the next batch; confirm block until the configured clean-up period elapses.

requirement: Cleanrooms and clean-air equipment are requalified periodically (Grade A/B at most every 6 months, C/D at most every 12 months) and after remedial actions or significant changes (air interruption, HVAC or design changes, final filter replacement).
system_implications: Hard stop: a step cannot start in a room/device whose requalification is overdue or flagged 'requalification required after change/remediation'; the maximum intervals are locked minimums in configuration.
verification_test: Set a Grade B room last requalified 6 months + 1 day ago; confirm step start is blocked; set a 'filter changed' flag and confirm block until requalification is recorded.

requirement: Cleanrooms are cleaned then disinfected per a written programme; residues are removed; more than one disinfectant type with different modes of action is used; a sporicide is applied periodically; effectiveness is monitored including shifts in flora or resistant organisms.
system_implications: Room cleaning/disinfection log records cleaning before disinfection, agent, lot and rotation; the system enforces rotation and sporicide frequency and shows the room's cleaning status at batch/step start; overdue cleaning blocks room use.
verification_test: Record disinfection without preceding cleaning; confirm it is flagged; exceed sporicide interval and confirm room status turns 'not ready'.

requirement: Disinfection is validated, including in-use expiry of prepared solutions. Disinfectants/detergents for Grade A/B are sterile before use (C/D where CCS requires); in-house dilutions are prepared to avoid contamination, monitored microbiologically, kept in cleaned (sterilised where applicable) containers and stored only for the defined period; ready-made agents may rely on CoA/CoC after vendor qualification.
system_implications: Disinfectant preparation record captures dilution date/time, container status, in-use expiry and microbial monitoring result; use in Grade A/B requires a sterile lot (CoA/CoC or in-house sterilisation record); expired dilutions are rejected at scan.
verification_test: Scan a non-sterile disinfectant lot for a Grade B task; confirm rejection; scan a dilution past its in-use expiry and confirm rejection.

requirement: Fumigation or vapour disinfection (e.g. VHP) of rooms requires a validated, understood agent and dispersion system.
system_implications: Room fumigation events are recorded with validated cycle ID and outcome; room status after fumigation is released only on a successful cycle record.
verification_test: Record a failed room VHP cycle; confirm the room remains unavailable for batch steps.

requirement: Process and equipment alarms are acknowledged and trended; review frequency follows criticality, with critical alarms reviewed immediately.
system_implications: eBMR ingests equipment/SCADA alarms for all batch equipment, classifies them by criticality from master data, requires immediate documented review of critical alarms before the step can continue, and lists all alarms in the batch report for trending.
verification_test: Raise a critical filler alarm during filling; confirm the step pauses until an authorised reviewer records an evaluation; confirm the alarm appears in the batch alarm summary.

requirement: Maintenance inside a cleanroom that cannot keep cleanliness/asepsis needs restricted access, defined work protocols, and consideration of extra cleaning, disinfection and EM; equipment sterilisation is done after full reassembly where possible.
system_implications: Recording an in-room maintenance event on a batch line inserts mandatory follow-up steps (additional cleaning/disinfection, extra EM samples, re-sterilisation of reassembled parts) before production resumes.
verification_test: Log in-cleanroom maintenance on the filler; confirm the system inserts cleaning, disinfection, EM and re-sterilisation tasks and blocks restart until completed.

requirement: Equipment cleaning is validated to remove residues that impair disinfectants and to minimise chemical, microbial and particulate contamination before disinfection.
system_implications: Equipment cleaning records must reference the validated cleaning procedure/version and cleaning status (clean, dirty-hold expiry, clean-hold expiry) is checked before use.
verification_test: Try to use equipment whose clean-hold time has expired; confirm block.

requirement: In aseptic processing both direct product-contact parts (e.g. filling needles, pumps) and indirect contact parts whose sterility is critical (e.g. stopper bowls, guides, sterilised components) are sterilised.
system_implications: Line set-up must list every direct and indirect product-contact part/kit and require a sterilisation load ID (or gamma certificate for SUS) for each, with sterile-hold expiry checked at assembly.
verification_test: Assemble a stopper bowl with no linked autoclave load; confirm set-up cannot be completed.

requirement: Sterilisers, HVAC (including filtration) and water systems are qualified, monitored and maintained on plan; return to use after maintenance is formally approved.
system_implications: Equipment status engine checks qualification validity, preventive-maintenance due date and 'released after maintenance' approval before an item can be used in a batch step.
verification_test: Complete maintenance on an autoclave without release approval; confirm the autoclave cannot be selected for a load.

requirement: Before unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment, the potential impact on product sterility is assessed and recorded.
system_implications: Unplanned maintenance on equipment flagged 'sterility-critical' requires a sterility-impact assessment record that is automatically linked to the in-process and adjacent batches.
verification_test: Open an unplanned work order on the depyrogenation tunnel during a batch; confirm the impact assessment is mandatory and appears in the batch review list.

requirement: Conveyors should not cross a Grade A/B partition to a lower grade unless continuously sterilised (e.g. tunnel). Particle counters and tubing are qualified (tubing typically no longer than 1 m, minimal bends, isokinetic heads in UDAF, close to critical point).
system_implications: EM integration must record the particle counter/probe ID for each monitoring location and verify the instrument's calibration/qualification is current for the batch window.
verification_test: Link particle data from a counter with expired calibration; confirm the batch EM summary flags it.

requirement: Utility controls are proportionate to risk, documented in the CCS; high-risk utilities include those contacting product, materials becoming product, or product-contact surfaces (e.g. rinse water, process gases, sterilising steam); critical parameters of high-risk utilities are trended.
system_implications: Master record identifies each high-risk utility point of use per step (WFI outlet, pure-steam header, gas drop); the batch record shows the utility status/trend flag for each point used, so an adverse trend or open excursion is visible at review.
verification_test: Mark the nitrogen supply with an open adverse-trend flag; confirm batches using that drop show a review item.

requirement: Water systems are designed and qualified (including seasonal variation) to prevent microbial, particulate and endotoxin contamination; water meets the pharmacopoeial monograph; flow stays turbulent and is monitored; WFI is made by distillation or an equivalent process and stored/circulated to minimise growth (e.g. continuous circulation above 70 C).
system_implications: When WFI is drawn for compounding or rinsing, the eBMR records outlet, draw time and volume and imports the loop temperature and flow values at draw time, flagging values outside validated ranges.
verification_test: Record a WFI draw while the loop temperature is below the validated minimum; confirm the draw is flagged for assessment.

requirement: Hydrophobic bacteria-retentive vent filters on WFI tanks should not contaminate; their integrity is tested before installation and after use, and condensation on them is prevented (e.g. heating).
system_implications: Utility status for WFI storage includes vent filter installation/removal integrity results; a failed post-use test creates an event linked to batches that used water during the filter's service period.
verification_test: Enter a failed post-use vent filter test; confirm the batches supplied during its service window are listed for impact assessment.

requirement: Water systems are sanitised/regenerated on a schedule and after out-of-limit results; chemical sanitisation is followed by validated rinsing; water is tested afterwards; chemical results are approved before return to use, and microbiological/endotoxin results should be within specification and approved before batches made with that water are considered for certification.
system_implications: The eBMR must tag every batch that used water drawn after a sanitisation event until the post-sanitisation micro/endotoxin results are approved, and block QP certification of those batches until then; water use before chemical release after sanitisation is blocked.
verification_test: Sanitise the WFI loop, draw water for a batch after chemical approval but before micro/endotoxin approval; confirm certification of that batch is blocked until the results are approved.

requirement: Water is monitored chemically and microbiologically per a CCS-based plan covering all outlets/points of use, with at least one representative sample every day of water used in manufacture; alert levels derive from qualification data and are reassessed; alert excursions are reviewed for isolated vs trend; every action-limit excursion is investigated for root cause and impact on products and processes.
system_implications: For each day of manufacture the batch record must show the water sample results for the points of use (or loop) supplying the batch; action-limit excursions automatically link to all batches that used water from the affected point/loop in the relevant period and block release pending investigation.
verification_test: Enter an action-limit TAMC result for outlet 12 on day D; confirm batches that drew from outlet 12 around day D are listed and blocked pending investigation.

requirement: WFI systems include continuous monitoring such as TOC and conductivity, with risk-based sensor locations.
system_implications: Batch record imports the continuous TOC and conductivity values for the WFI loop over each draw window and flags excursions.
verification_test: Replay a conductivity spike during a draw; confirm a flagged excursion on the batch.

requirement: Pure steam used as a direct sterilant comes from purified feed water, has no contaminating additives, its condensate meets the WFI monograph (microbial testing not mandatory), is sampled regularly, and is periodically checked for non-condensable gases, dryness and superheat.
system_implications: Autoclave/SIP pre-use readiness checks that the supplying pure-steam system's latest condensate result and NCG/dryness/superheat tests are within limits and not overdue; otherwise the cycle is flagged.
verification_test: Set the steam dryness test overdue; confirm the autoclave run is flagged as using unverified steam.

requirement: Gases directly contacting product or primary container surfaces have specified chemical, particulate, microbial, oil and water quality meeting pharmacopoeia or product requirements.
system_implications: Gas supply (bulk tank, cylinder or generator) used in a batch is recorded with lot/CoA or generator quality status; the step blocks if gas quality release status is not current.
verification_test: Connect a nitrogen cylinder with no released CoA; confirm the overlay step blocks.

requirement: Process gases for aseptic use pass a sterilising-grade filter (max nominal 0.22 um) at point of use; filters used on a batch basis (e.g. overlay gas) or as product vessel vents are integrity tested and the results reviewed during batch certification; tubing downstream of the final filter is sterilised; gas is periodically monitored microbially at point of use.
system_implications: Gas filters and vessel vent filters are batch components with ID, pore rating, sterilisation load, and post-use (and where defined pre-use) integrity results; a missing or failed result is a release blocker shown in the QP review.
verification_test: Complete a batch without the nitrogen overlay filter post-use test; confirm certification is blocked.

requirement: Backflow from vacuum/pressure systems into product is prevented; hydraulic, heating and cooling equipment is outside the filling room where possible, spillage is contained, and leaks posing product risk are detectable.
system_implications: Leak-detection or backflow-prevention alarms from lyophiliser/filler utilities are captured as batch events requiring assessment.
verification_test: Trigger a silicone-oil leak alarm on the lyophiliser during a cycle; confirm it appears as an open batch event.

requirement: Enough qualified, trained and experienced staff are available for sterile manufacture and the specific technologies used; only the minimum staff are present in cleanrooms, and the maximum operator number per cleanroom is set, documented and considered in qualification and APS.
system_implications: Room master data holds the maximum operator count (not exceeding the number qualified in the latest APS); the eBMR counts personnel entries (access control or gowning log) per room and alarms/blocks when exceeded.
verification_test: Badge in a fifth operator into a Grade B room with a limit of four; confirm an alert and a batch event.

requirement: Everyone who enters cleanrooms (including cleaners, maintenance and monitoring staff) receives regular training, gowning qualification and assessment covering microbiology basics, hygiene, cleanroom practice, contamination control and (for Grade B entry/Grade A intervention) aseptic technique and patient-safety consequences; depth depends on role criticality.
system_implications: Training/qualification checks at e-signature must apply to all roles that record work in cleanrooms (operators, EM samplers, cleaners, engineers), keyed to the grade of the area and the criticality of the task.
verification_test: Have a maintenance technician without current cleanroom training sign an in-room maintenance step; confirm the signature is refused.

requirement: Grade A/B staff are trained in aseptic gowning and behaviour; gowning compliance is assessed initially and reassessed at least annually, visually and microbiologically (gloved fingers, forearms, chest, hood/mask/forehead); unsupervised A/B access is limited to people who passed gowning assessment and took part in a successful APS.
system_implications: Before an operator can sign any Grade A/B step unsupervised, the system verifies: gowning qualification passed within the last 12 months, aseptic training current, and participation in a successful APS covering this line/process; failures route to 'supervised only' mode or block.
verification_test: Use an operator whose gowning requalification is 12 months + 1 day old; confirm Grade B step sign-off is blocked. Use an operator with no successful APS; confirm unsupervised sign-off is blocked.

requirement: Unqualified people should not enter Grade B or Grade A in operation; exceptional entry follows a written procedure, with an authorised person supervising and assessing the impact on area cleanliness; such access is assessed and recorded under the PQS.
system_implications: Provide an 'exceptional supervised entry' record (person, reason, time in/out, supervising authorised person, cleanliness impact assessment) that links to every batch in progress in that area and appears in the batch exception report.
verification_test: Record a supervised contractor entry into Grade B during filling; confirm the supervisor's qualification is checked, the impact assessment is mandatory and the entry shows in batch review.

requirement: A disqualification system removes operators from cleanroom work or unsupervised entry based on ongoing assessment, adverse personnel-monitoring trends, or implication in a failed APS; retraining and requalification are completed before any further aseptic involvement, and for Grade B entry/Grade A intervention requalification should consider participation in a successful APS.
system_implications: Operator qualification status must support 'disqualified' set automatically by triggers (PM trend rule, failed-APS linkage) or manually by QA; disqualified users cannot sign aseptic steps; requalification requires linked retraining, gowning assessment and (configurable, default on) a successful APS.
verification_test: Mark an APS as failed; confirm all participating operators flip to disqualified and cannot sign Grade A/B steps until requalification records (incl. successful APS) are linked.

requirement: Staff report health conditions that could shed abnormal contaminants, with procedures defining actions; staff who have worked with human/animal tissue or other microbial cultures, or on other quality-risk activities, only enter clean areas after documented, effective decontamination/entry procedures.
system_implications: Gowning/entry workflow should include a fitness-to-enter self-declaration and a declaration of recent work with tissues/cultures, with a mandatory documented decontamination step when declared.
verification_test: Declare recent culture work at entry; confirm entry is blocked until a decontamination record is completed.

requirement: Personal items (watches, jewellery, make-up, phones) are not allowed in clean areas; manufacturer-supplied electronic devices dedicated to cleanroom use (e.g. tablets) are acceptable if designed for cleaning/disinfection suitable for the grade, and their use and disinfection are covered by the CCS.
system_implications: Hardware constraint on the eBMR itself: in-cleanroom terminals/tablets/scanners must be dedicated, registered assets rated for the grade's disinfectants; the system should log device disinfection before entry and refuse sessions from unregistered devices inside classified areas.
verification_test: Attempt to log into a Grade B workstation profile from an unregistered tablet; confirm refusal; confirm a registered tablet requires a disinfection record at transfer-in.

requirement: Gowning and hand washing follow written procedures; garments suit the grade (Grade B/A: sterile suit, hood enclosing all hair, mask, eye cover, sterile gloves double-layered over sleeves, sterile over-boots; Grade C: covered hair, high-neck suit gathered at wrists, disinfected shoes; Grade D: covered hair, general protective suit; extra items in C/D where CCS requires); garments are visually checked for cleanliness and integrity before and after donning and on exit; sterilised garments/eye covers are checked for sterilisation, hold time and intact packaging; reusable garments are replaced when damaged or at the qualified frequency.
system_implications: Gowning log (per entry) captures garment/sterile-pack lot, sterilisation expiry, packaging-intact check, pre/post-donning visual check and exit integrity check; expired or unsterilised packs are rejected at scan.
verification_test: Scan a sterile gown pack past its sterile hold expiry; confirm rejection; skip the exit integrity check and confirm the entry record stays open.

requirement: Each Grade A/B entry uses fresh sterilised garments (including eye covers and masks) of the right size; the maximum wear time of a sterile gown during a shift is defined in garment qualification; gloves are disinfected regularly during work and damaged garments/gloves are changed immediately.
system_implications: Per-operator gown-wear timer from gowning time with warning before and alert at the qualified maximum; glove disinfection prompts at the defined interval; garment/glove change events are recorded and damaged-garment events during exposed-product activities raise an assessment.
verification_test: Keep an operator in Grade B past the maximum gown wear time; confirm alert and a batch event; record a torn glove during filling and confirm an assessment is required.

requirement: Reusable cleanroom clothing is laundered in a segregated, qualified process, inspected after washing, and garment management defines a maximum number of laundry and sterilisation cycles.
system_implications: If garments are tracked (e.g. RFID), the gowning scan checks the garment's cycle count against the qualified maximum and rejects over-cycled garments.
verification_test: Scan a garment at cycle count = max + 1; confirm rejection.

requirement: Non-critical activities in clean areas are minimised, especially during aseptic work; movements are slow and controlled; aseptic technique is maintained at all times; movement near the critical zone is restricted and first-air paths are not obstructed.
system_implications: eBMR screens in Grade A/B should minimise operator data-entry burden near the critical zone (e.g. terminals placed outside first-air path, voice/scan entry, batch entry after the activity where allowed); aseptic behaviour observations by supervisors can be captured as batch-linked records.
verification_test: Review the station layout specification per line; confirm no mandatory data entry requires reaching across the critical zone.

requirement: For terminally sterilised products, components and materials are prepared in at least Grade D; if the product is at high or unusual contamination risk (supports growth, long hold before filling, not mostly in closed vessels) preparation is in at least Grade C, as is preparation of ointments, creams, suspensions and emulsions before terminal sterilisation; primary containers/components are cleaned by validated processes controlling particles, endotoxin and bioburden.
system_implications: Product master carries a CCS risk flag ('unusual risk') and dosage-form type that raise the minimum preparation grade from D to C automatically; component washing steps reference the validated washing process and record its parameters.
verification_test: Flag a TS product as growth-supporting; confirm the master record rejects a Grade D compounding room.

requirement: Filling of products for terminal sterilisation is done in at least Grade C; where the CCS shows unusual environmental risk (slow filling, wide-necked containers, exposure beyond a few seconds before closing) filling is in Grade A with at least Grade C background.
system_implications: Filling step grade requirement is derived from product/container risk flags (C, or A-in-C); room check at step start enforces it.
verification_test: Set container type 'wide-neck'; confirm the filling step demands Grade A zone with Grade C background.

requirement: For terminally sterilised products, bulk solution is passed where possible through a microorganism-retaining filter to lower bioburden and particles before filling, and a maximum permissible time between preparation and filling is set.
system_implications: The eBMR runs a preparation-start-to-filling-end timer against the product's validated maximum and records the bioburden-reduction filter ID; exceeding the limit is a hard stop requiring deviation.
verification_test: Delay filling beyond the configured prep-to-fill limit; confirm an automatic deviation and a block on continuing without QA decision.

name: Grade assignment examples - terminally sterilised products (Table 3)
values: Grade A (with at least Grade C background): filling when product is unusually at risk. Grade C: solution preparation when unusually at risk; routine filling. Grade D: making up solutions and readying components ahead of filling.

name: Grade assignment examples - aseptic preparation and processing (Table 4)
values: Grade A: aseptic assembly of filling equipment; aseptic connections downstream of the final sterilising filter (SIP preferred); aseptic compounding/mixing; replenishing sterile bulk, containers and closures; removing and cooling unwrapped items from sterilisers; staging/conveying unwrapped sterile primary components on the line; aseptic filling, ampoule sealing, vial closure, transfer of open or part-stoppered vials; lyophiliser loading. Grade B: background to Grade A (non-isolator); protected conveying/staging of items for introduction to Grade A. Grade C: preparation (incl. sampling and dispensing) of solutions that will be filtered. Grade D: equipment cleaning; handling of cleaned components/equipment; assembly of cleaned items under HEPA airflow before sterilisation; assembly of closed sterilised SUS using intrinsic sterile connectors.

requirement: The aseptic process is clearly defined, its risks assessed and controlled, with CCS-defined acceptance criteria, monitoring and effectiveness review and formally documented residual risks; contamination precautions apply from preparing the aseptic environment through all stages until the product is sealed; particle- and fibre-generating materials are minimised in cleanrooms.
system_implications: Master record for an aseptic product must map each step to its CCS control and acceptance criterion; the eBMR itself should eliminate paper in Grade A/B (paper is a fibre source), using cleanroom-rated devices instead of printed records.
verification_test: Audit an aseptic master record; confirm every step from environment preparation to final seal has a CCS control reference; confirm no printed forms are required inside Grade A/B.

requirement: Barrier systems, robotics and automation (e.g. dry heat tunnels, automated lyophiliser loading, SIP) should be considered to reduce critical Grade A interventions; aseptic manipulations are minimised by pre-assembled, pre-sterilised equipment and sterilisation in place where feasible.
system_implications: Master record supports SIP/pre-assembled kit steps as the default path; manual aseptic assembly steps are flagged in the master record design review as higher-risk items needing justification.
verification_test: Create a master record with a manual aseptic assembly step; confirm the design-review checklist requests a justification.

requirement: Where the final formulation cannot be filtered: all product- and component-contact equipment is sterilised before use, all raw materials or intermediates are sterilised and added aseptically, and bulk solutions or intermediates are sterilised.
system_implications: Products flagged 'non-filterable' force every material addition step to require evidence of sterilisation (in-house load ID or supplier sterile CoA) and aseptic addition in Grade A; equipment sterilisation evidence is mandatory for all contact items.
verification_test: For a non-filterable suspension, add an excipient lot without sterile status; confirm block.

requirement: Unwrapping, assembly and preparation of sterilised items with direct or indirect product contact, line set-up and filling are aseptic operations in Grade A with Grade B background (isolator background per 4.20); non-filtered, non-terminally-sterilised exposed ointments, creams, suspensions and emulsions are prepared and filled in Grade A/B.
system_implications: Set-up and assembly steps are typed 'aseptic' in the master record, which forces Grade A zone + qualified background checks, operator aseptic qualification checks and inclusion in the intervention/EM linkage.
verification_test: Attempt to perform stopper-bowl assembly in a step typed as non-aseptic; confirm master record validation rejects it.

requirement: Aseptic connections are made in Grade A with Grade B background unless they are subsequently sterilised in place or made with intrinsic sterile connection devices designed to limit environmental contamination; aseptic connections are assessed and their effectiveness verified.
system_implications: Each connection step records the connection method (open aseptic in Grade A, post-connection SIP with cycle ID, or intrinsic sterile connector with device lot/type), location and operator; open connections outside Grade A are blocked.
verification_test: Record an open aseptic connection in Grade C without SIP; confirm block; record a sterile connector with lot and confirm acceptance.

requirement: An authorised list of allowed, qualified interventions (inherent and corrective) exists, each designed to minimise contamination risk (airflow, critical surfaces, product), using engineering solutions and sterile tools, first evaluated by risk management and APS and kept current.
system_implications: Intervention catalogue master data per line: ID, type (inherent/corrective), procedure reference, APS in which it was qualified, qualification date, allowed max count/duration; the operator selects from this list when recording an intervention.
verification_test: Record an intervention; confirm only catalogue entries qualified in a valid APS for this line are selectable.

requirement: Non-qualified interventions are used only exceptionally, with the quality unit's authorisation and risk consideration; they are risk-assessed, recorded, fully investigated under the PQS, thoroughly assessed by QA and taken into account at batch disposition.
system_implications: Recording an intervention not in the catalogue requires a real-time QA authorisation e-signature, auto-creates a deviation/investigation, flags affected units/time window, and places a mandatory QA disposition item on the batch that blocks certification until closed.
verification_test: Record an 'other' intervention; confirm QA sign-off is required before continuing, a deviation is created automatically, and the batch cannot be certified while it is open.

requirement: Every intervention and line stoppage is recorded in the batch record with time, duration and the operators involved.
system_implications: Intervention/stoppage log with start and end timestamps (duration computed, not typed), intervention catalogue ID, affected zone/filling position, operators involved, units removed, and linkage to concurrent EM/particle data; stoppages can be captured automatically from line PLC state.
verification_test: Stop the filler via PLC for 4 minutes; confirm a stoppage entry is auto-created with timestamps, and the batch cannot proceed to review until operators and reason are completed.

requirement: Validated maximum times apply to: holding between cleaning, drying and sterilisation of equipment/components/containers; holding of sterilised equipment/components/containers before use and during filling/assembly; holding a decontaminated RABS/isolator before use.
system_implications: Timestamp-driven hold-time checks: cleaned-to-sterilised (dirty/clean hold), sterilisation-end-to-use-end (sterile hold, also through the filling run), and bio-decontamination-end-to-aseptic-start; any exceedance blocks use and raises a deviation.
verification_test: Use a stopper load whose sterile hold expires mid-fill; confirm the system alarms at expiry and requires deviation; start filling after isolator decon hold expiry and confirm block.

requirement: A validated maximum time applies from start of product preparation to its sterilisation or sterilising filtration and on to the end of aseptic filling, set per product considering composition and storage method; sterilised product also has a maximum hold before filling.
system_implications: Product-specific timers: prep-start to filtration/sterilisation start, prep-start to end of filling (overall), and filtration/sterilisation end to filling start; storage condition during hold is recorded; limits are product master data with validation reference.
verification_test: Configure 24 h prep-to-fill-end; run past 24 h; confirm hard stop/deviation; check that the storage temperature log for the hold vessel is attached.

requirement: Aseptic processing time and filling time are each limited to a validated maximum; the APS should be long enough to challenge the process, and should cover maximum permitted holding times of exposed sterile product and equipment.
system_implications: The eBMR tracks aseptic processing start/end and filling start/end and compares them with the validated maximum and with the longest duration qualified by APS for the line; exceeding either blocks continuation without QA decision.
verification_test: Configure max filling time 30 h with APS-qualified 32 h; run 30.5 h; confirm deviation is raised at 30 h.

requirement: Aseptic operations, including APS, are regularly observed by people with specific aseptic expertise to verify correct performance and operator behaviour and to correct poor practice.
system_implications: Provide a batch-linked aseptic observation record (observer, qualification, time window, findings, operators coached); overdue observation frequency per line is visible in line readiness.
verification_test: Create an observation record by a user without aseptic-expert role; confirm refusal.

requirement: Open primary containers stay under Grade A with the background appropriate to the technology; final containers are closed by validated methods.
system_implications: Closure step records the validated closing method/equipment and key settings; open-container transfer steps are bound to Grade A zones.
verification_test: Try to route open vials through a zone not classified Grade A in the line map; confirm master record rejects it.

requirement: For fusion-sealed containers (BFS, FFS, SVP/LVP bags, glass or plastic ampoules), seal-critical parameters are determined, controlled and monitored during operation; glass ampoules, BFS units and fusion-sealed containers of 100 ml or less undergo 100 percent integrity testing by validated methods; over 100 ml, reduced sampling may be accepted only with scientific justification and demonstrated process consistency; visual inspection is not an acceptable integrity test.
system_implications: For fusion-sealed presentations the eBMR requires seal parameter records (e.g. heater temperatures, dwell) and a 100 percent CCI step (units tested, passes, rejects by reason) for containers up to 100 ml; the CCI method field cannot be set to visual inspection; reduced sampling for more than 100 ml needs a referenced justification.
verification_test: Configure a 2 ml ampoule product with sampled CCI; confirm master record rejects it; attempt to choose 'visual inspection' as CCI method; confirm it is not allowed.

requirement: Non-fusion closures (e.g. stoppered and crimped vials, syringes) are integrity-tested on samples by validated methods under a scientifically justified sampling plan based on container-closure knowledge, supplier management and component specifications.
system_implications: CCI sampling step with configurable plan (sample size, method, reference to justification), results per unit, and release linkage; failure triggers investigation and blocks release.
verification_test: Record one CCI sample failure; confirm deviation creation and certification block.

requirement: Containers sealed under vacuum are tested for vacuum retention after a predetermined period before certification and during shelf life; CCI validation considers transport stresses such as decompression and extreme temperatures.
system_implications: For vacuum-sealed presentations (e.g. lyophilised vials under vacuum), the eBMR schedules a vacuum-retention test after the configured waiting period and blocks certification until the result is recorded and passing.
verification_test: Attempt to certify a vacuum-stoppered lyo batch before the vacuum-retention test date; confirm block.

requirement: Particle-generating crimping is separated with extraction; capping of aseptically filled vials is either an aseptic process with sterilised caps or a clean process outside the aseptic area in which vials are protected by Grade A up to leaving the aseptic area and then by Grade A air supply (background at least Grade D) until crimped; manual capping is done in Grade A (isolator or Grade A in Grade B); interventions at capping avoid direct vial contact.
system_implications: Line configuration records the capping mode (aseptic/clean-with-Grade-A-air); the eBMR records the transfer time from stoppering to crimping, the capping station's Grade A air supply status and cap lots (with sterilisation evidence where capping is aseptic); manual capping steps require a Grade A location.
verification_test: Configure clean-process capping and simulate loss of Grade A air supply at the capper; confirm a batch event is raised for the affected vials.

requirement: When capping is a clean process under Grade A air, vials with missing or displaced stoppers are rejected before capping using qualified automated stopper-height detection.
system_implications: eBMR captures stopper-height detector qualification status, start-of-batch (and periodic) challenge results, and the count of vials rejected for stopper height; these rejects enter the batch reconciliation.
verification_test: Run a batch without the stopper-height challenge; confirm the capping step cannot start; confirm reject counts are pulled into reconciliation.

requirement: Every filled parenteral container is individually inspected for extraneous contamination and defects; defect classes and criticality are set in qualification using patient risk and route of administration; defect types are categorised and batch performance analysed; batches with unusual defect levels versus routine/trend data are investigated; a maintained defect library supports training.
system_implications: 100 percent inspection step records inspected, accepted and rejected counts by defect code (from a controlled defect library with criticality critical/major/minor); per-defect alert limits derived from historical data trigger investigation automatically.
verification_test: Enter particle-reject counts above the product alert limit; confirm an investigation is opened and the batch is blocked for certification.

requirement: Critical defects should not be found in later sampling/inspection of accepted containers; finding one indicates possible failure of the original inspection and triggers an investigation.
system_implications: Post-inspection acceptance sampling (e.g. AQL) records defects by class; any critical defect in the accepted population automatically opens an investigation, blocks release and prompts a re-inspection decision.
verification_test: Record one critical defect (e.g. cracked vial) in the AQL sample; confirm automatic investigation and certification block.

requirement: Manual inspection runs under controlled illumination and background at a controlled, qualified rate; inspectors are qualified at least annually (with their usual corrective lenses) using defect-library sets and worst-case conditions (time, conveyor speed, container size, fatigue), including eyesight checks; distractions are minimised and frequent breaks taken.
system_implications: Before an inspector signs on to a manual inspection station, the eBMR checks VI qualification (last 12 months) and eyesight check validity; the station records illuminance/background check, inspection rate or throughput, and enforces maximum continuous inspection time before a break.
verification_test: Assign an inspector whose VI qualification is 13 months old; confirm refusal; exceed the configured continuous inspection period; confirm a break prompt/lock.

requirement: Automated inspection is validated to detect known defects at least as well as manual inspection, and is challenged with representative defect sets before start-up and at regular intervals during the batch.
system_implications: The AVI step requires a passing challenge-set run (set ID, expected vs detected per defect) at start and at the configured interval; a failed interim challenge flags all units inspected since the last passing challenge for re-inspection.
verification_test: Record a failed mid-batch challenge; confirm the units since the prior pass are placed on hold for re-inspection.

requirement: Inspection results are recorded; defect types and numbers are trended and reject levels trended statistically; adverse trends trigger investigation including impact on product already on the market.
system_implications: Defect data are stored as structured counts per defect code per batch so SPC trending across batches is possible; an adverse trend signal opens an investigation with a mandatory 'market impact' field.
verification_test: Load 10 batches with rising glass-particle rejects; confirm the trend rule fires and the investigation form requires market-impact assessment.

requirement: Terminal sterilisation is preferred where possible; otherwise post-aseptic terminal heat treatment combined with aseptic processing should be considered; non-pharmacopoeial methods or non-aqueous products need particular attention, with heat the method of choice.
system_implications: Product master records the sterility-assurance route (terminal / aseptic / aseptic + post-aseptic heat treatment) with a justification reference; this selects the appropriate master record template.
verification_test: Create an aseptic product without a sterilisation-route justification; confirm the master cannot be approved.

requirement: Sterilisation equipment and cycles are chosen on scientific data; all parameters are defined and critical ones controlled, monitored and recorded; all sterilisation processes are validated (including product composition, storage and maximum time from preparation start to sterilisation) and routine operating parameters and load patterns are followed.
system_implications: Each sterilisation step references a validated cycle recipe (with version) whose critical parameters and ranges are master data; imported cycle data are compared to them automatically; the prep-to-sterilisation time is checked against the validated maximum.
verification_test: Run a cycle under a recipe version not linked to a current validation; confirm the load is flagged as non-conforming.

requirement: Validated loading patterns exist for every sterilisation process (considering maximum and minimum loads) and are periodically revalidated; heat sterilisation cycles are revalidated at least annually for worst-case load patterns, others at a CCS-justified frequency.
system_implications: Load building requires selecting a validated load pattern and recording actual item types and quantities, checked against the pattern's min/max; the system blocks a load pattern or steriliser whose worst-case revalidation is older than 12 months (or the CCS interval).
verification_test: Build a load with more items than the pattern maximum; confirm block. Expire the annual revalidation; confirm the pattern cannot be selected.

requirement: Mechanisms detect any sterilisation cycle not conforming to validated parameters; any failed cycle, or one deviating from the validated process (e.g. longer or shorter phases), is investigated.
system_implications: The eBMR compares each imported cycle (phase durations, temperatures/pressures, F0 where used) against the validated recipe; any failure or deviation auto-quarantines the load, prevents consumption of its items and opens an investigation.
verification_test: Import a cycle with a heating phase 20 percent longer than validated but passing exposure; confirm it is still flagged as deviating and the load is quarantined.

requirement: BIs may support validation; they are stored and used per the supplier's instructions; where BIs support validation or routine monitoring (e.g. EO), positive controls are tested for each cycle; BI handling should not contaminate other processes; BI results alone should not override critical parameters; BI suppliers are qualified, transport/storage controlled, and each new BI lot is verified for population, purity and identity (D/Z values may come from the supplier certificate).
system_implications: Where a cycle uses BIs, the record captures BI lot (with incoming-verification status), positions, exposure, incubation results and the positive-control result; a passing BI cannot clear a cycle that failed physical parameters.
verification_test: Enter passing BIs for a cycle with a failed temperature parameter; confirm the load remains rejected; enter a BI lot without population/identity verification and confirm refusal.

requirement: Sterilised and non-sterilised products, equipment and components are clearly distinguishable; carriers such as baskets and trays are labelled or electronically tracked with product name, batch number and sterilised/not-sterilised status; process indicators (autoclave tape, irradiation dots) only show exposure, not sterility.
system_implications: Electronic tracking of every load carrier and item: ID, product/batch, state (to be sterilised, sterilised-pending review, released, rejected); the scanner at point of use refuses items not in 'released sterile' state; indicator checks are recorded but never used alone as release evidence.
verification_test: Scan a tray whose cycle is not yet reviewed at the Grade A entry; confirm refusal; scan an item from a quarantined load and confirm refusal.

requirement: A sterilisation record exists for each run, each cycle has a unique identifier, and conformity of the records is reviewed and approved as part of batch certification/release.
system_implications: Every item consumed in the batch resolves to a unique cycle ID; the QP/QA review lists all cycle IDs contributing to the batch (product, components, equipment, garments where relevant) with their conformity status, and certification is blocked if any is not approved.
verification_test: Consume stoppers from a cycle whose record is unreviewed; confirm the batch cannot be certified and the cycle appears as an open item.

requirement: Items are sterilised by validated methods and protected against recontamination; if not used immediately they are held in sealed packaging for no longer than an established maximum hold time; sealing precedes sterilisation; packaging is qualified and its sealing validated, including maximum time before sterilisation and sterile shelf life; the integrity of each item's sterile barrier is checked before use. Multi-layer sterile packs may be stored outside cleanrooms if justified.
system_implications: Per item/load: packing time, sterilisation time and sterile expiry are tracked; packing-to-sterilisation and sterile-hold limits are enforced; at point of use the operator must confirm packaging integrity per item (or reject it), and damaged packs are recorded.
verification_test: Sterilise a pack after its packing-to-sterilisation limit; confirm the load is flagged; at use, record 'integrity not OK' and confirm the item is rejected and replaced.

requirement: Sealed sterilised items enter Grade A via validated methods (airlocks, pass-throughs, RTP) with disinfection of the outer packaging shown to be effective; non-product-contact items needed for aseptic work that cannot be sterilised undergo validated disinfection and transfer, are protected afterwards, and are included in the EM programme.
system_implications: Transfer records for sterile packs capture outer-layer disinfection (agent, contact time) and route; non-sterilisable items (e.g. monitors, tools) require a validated disinfection record and are listed as EM locations/surfaces for the batch.
verification_test: Transfer a non-sterilisable device into Grade A without a disinfection entry; confirm block; confirm it appears in the batch surface-sampling plan.

requirement: Each heat sterilisation cycle is recorded (electronically or hardcopy) with accurate, precise equipment; control and monitoring have safeguards/redundancy (e.g. duplex probes on independent control and monitoring systems) to detect non-conforming cycles and abort or fail them; probe positions are set and verified in validation.
system_implications: Cycle import must include data from both the control and the independent monitoring/recording channel, their probe IDs and positions, and the controller's pass/abort status; a discrepancy between channels beyond tolerance fails the cycle review.
verification_test: Import a cycle where control and independent probes differ by more than the tolerance; confirm the cycle is flagged non-conforming.

requirement: Sterilising time starts only when the whole load has reached the required temperature (for load-probe-controlled cycles the load probe is within range before the cycle starts); after the high-temperature phase the load is protected from recontamination during cooling and any cooling fluid or gas contacting product or sterilised items is sterilised.
system_implications: Automated cycle review checks equilibration before exposure timing and records cooling medium type with its sterilisation evidence (e.g. sterile-filtered air break, sterilised spray-cooling water for terminal sterilisation autoclaves).
verification_test: Import a cycle where exposure timing starts before the coldest probe reaches set point; confirm failure flag.

requirement: Where parametric release is authorised, a robust, periodically reviewed system covers lifecycle validation and routine process monitoring (see Annex 17).
system_implications: Product master flag 'parametric release authorised' with authorisation reference; the release workflow then replaces the sterility test with a mandatory, complete review of all critical sterilisation parameters and load records, and any parameter failure prevents parametric release.
verification_test: For a parametric-release product, enter a cycle with one critical parameter out of range; confirm the batch cannot be released parametrically.

requirement: Moist-heat sterilisation covers steam and superheated-water (cascade/immersion) systems. Items other than sealed product containers are dry and packed in a barrier allowing air removal and steam penetration; load dryness is confirmed visually as part of cycle acceptance; porous cycles are monitored and recorded by time, temperature and pressure; each item is inspected on unloading for damage, packaging integrity and moisture, and unfit items are removed and investigated.
system_implications: Autoclave unload step: mandatory load dryness check and per-item (or exception-based) inspection for damage/wet packs/packaging breach; rejected items are removed from inventory and an investigation is opened automatically; the load cannot be released without the unload inspection record.
verification_test: Record a wet pack at unloading; confirm the item is rejected, an investigation opens and the remaining load release requires QA review.

requirement: Pre-vacuum autoclaves record chamber-drain temperature throughout sterilisation (load probes optional but control tied to load validation); SIP records temperature at condensate drains; porous-cycle acceptance covers equilibration time, exposure time, pressure-temperature correlation and min/max exposure temperature; fluid cycles use temperature, time and/or F0; critical parameters have defined limits and tolerances in routine cycle acceptance.
system_implications: Automated cycle acceptance evaluates drain temperature over the whole exposure, equilibration time, exposure time, saturated-steam pressure/temperature agreement, min/max temperature band and (fluid loads) achieved F0 against validated limits and tolerances; the result and raw data are attached to the load record.
verification_test: Import a porous cycle where measured pressure does not correspond to saturated steam at the drain temperature; confirm failure.

requirement: Sterilisers with a vacuum phase, or returning to sub-ambient pressure after sterilisation, are leak-tested periodically, normally weekly.
system_implications: Steriliser readiness check blocks loads if the last passing vacuum leak test is older than the configured interval (default 7 days).
verification_test: Set last leak test 8 days ago; confirm the autoclave cannot be used for a load.

requirement: Air removal before and during sterilisation should be assured for processes with air purging (porous loads, lyophiliser chambers): autoclaves run an air-removal test cycle (normally daily) or use an air detector; loads are designed for air removal and free drainage.
system_implications: First porous load of each day requires a passing air-removal (Bowie-Dick type) test that day, or a functional air-detector result on each cycle; otherwise loads are blocked or flagged.
verification_test: Start a porous load without a same-day air-removal test on an autoclave lacking an air detector; confirm block.

requirement: Terminal sterilisation of non-rigid containers (BFS, FFS, bags) avoids distortion through cycle design (pressure, heating/cooling rates, loading); superheated-water fluid-load autoclaves should reach all contact points, are routinely checked for blocked nozzles and debris-free drains, and routine probes correlate with worst-case positions from load mapping.
system_implications: Pre-cycle checklist for superheated-water autoclaves records nozzle and drain checks; post-cycle step records container deformation/leak inspection for non-rigid containers; routine probe positions are fixed master data linked to the mapping study.
verification_test: Skip the nozzle/drain check; confirm the terminal sterilisation cycle cannot be started in the eBMR.

requirement: SIP systems (fixed pipework, vessels, lyophiliser chambers) are validated so all parts are treated; routine monitoring of temperature, pressure and time occurs at locations correlated with the slowest-heating points; after SIP the system stays integral and, where needed, under positive pressure or behind a sterilising vent filter until use.
system_implications: SIP record includes each monitored location's temperature/pressure/time against limits, cycle ID and result; post-SIP the eBMR tracks integrity status (positive pressure trend or vent filter ID) and a maximum post-SIP hold time until product use; loss of pressure invalidates the SIP.
verification_test: Import a post-SIP pressure trend that drops to ambient before use; confirm the SIP status becomes invalid and product transfer is blocked.

requirement: Dry-heat sterilisation/depyrogenation delivers reproducible lethality/endotoxin removal within limits; tunnels maintain pressure differentials and airflow protecting the Grade A zone, supplied through at least HEPA filters integrity-tested periodically (at least twice yearly, text: 'biannually'); tunnel parts touching sterilised components are sterilised or disinfected; critical parameters include belt speed/dwell time, min and max temperatures, heat penetration, heat distribution and airflow/DP profiles.
system_implications: For each batch the tunnel run record (belt speed or dwell time, zone temperatures min/max, DP profile vs limits, alarms) is attached to the container lot; the tunnel's HEPA integrity test currency is checked at batch start; any excursion quarantines containers processed in that window.
verification_test: Import a tunnel trace with a 5-minute hot-zone dip below minimum; confirm containers passing through in that window are identified and quarantined.

requirement: Thermal depyrogenation is validated to give a suitable Fh and at least a 3 log10 endotoxin reduction (which also covers sterilisation); endotoxin-spiked validation containers are representative and fully reconciled, with quantification and recovery demonstrated.
system_implications: Depyrogenation cycle master data holds the validated Fh minimum; where the controller calculates Fh the eBMR compares it; spiked-container validation runs are recorded as non-product runs with a full reconciliation so spiked units can never enter a batch.
verification_test: Record a validation run with 1 spiked container unreconciled; confirm the tunnel cannot be released to production.

requirement: Dry-heat ovens remain at positive pressure to lower-grade areas through sterilisation and post-sterilisation hold (unless packaging integrity is kept), with HEPA-filtered air; critical parameters include temperature, exposure time, chamber overpressure, air speed and quality, heat penetration and distribution, and load pattern including min/max loads.
system_implications: Oven cycle record includes temperature, exposure time and chamber differential pressure through the hold phase until unloading, plus the validated load pattern; loss of overpressure during hold flags unwrapped items as non-sterile.
verification_test: Import an oven cycle with overpressure lost during the cool-down hold for an unwrapped load; confirm the load is rejected.

requirement: Radiation sterilisation is mainly for heat-sensitive items (ionising radiation per Annex 12), with validation considering product and package density variation; ultraviolet irradiation is not an acceptable sterilisation method.
