system_implications: The sterilisation-method list must not offer UV as a sterilising method (UV may only be recorded as a surface-bioburden reduction aid); irradiated materials (e.g. gamma-sterilised SUS, stoppers) are recorded with irradiation certificate, dose range and processing lot.
verification_test: Try to set a component's sterilisation method to UV; confirm the option is unavailable.

requirement: Ethylene oxide is used only when no other method is practicable; validation shows no product damage and that degassing time/conditions reduce residual EO and reaction products to defined limits; direct gas-to-organism contact is essential, so occluded organisms and packaging nature/porosity/quantity matter; loads are pre-conditioned to the required humidity and temperature (using suitable-quality steam) with conditioning time balanced against minimising time before sterilisation.
system_implications: EO-sterilised materials require the EO cycle record (preconditioning time, temperature, RH), a justification reference that no alternative is practicable, and residual EO/reaction-product results within limits before use.
verification_test: Attempt to issue an EO-sterilised component lot without residual EO results; confirm block.

requirement: Every EO cycle is monitored with suitable BIs in adequate number at validated worst-case locations (with positive controls per cycle); critical parameters considered include EO concentration, pressure, amount of gas, RH, temperature and exposure time.
system_implications: EO load release requires: cycle parameter record (gas concentration, pressure, gas mass, RH, temperature, exposure time), BI results for each defined location, positive control growth confirmation; missing or positive BI blocks release.
verification_test: Enter an EO cycle with one BI location missing; confirm the load cannot be released.

requirement: After EO sterilisation the load is aerated (in chamber, aeration chamber or room) so EO and reaction products desorb to predetermined levels, the aeration phase being validated.
system_implications: Aeration start/end, location and conditions are recorded; the system prevents release of EO-sterilised items before the validated minimum aeration time has elapsed.
verification_test: Attempt to release an EO load 2 hours before minimum aeration completes; confirm block.

requirement: Products that cannot be sterilised in their final container are sterile-filtered through a sterile, validated sterilising-grade filter (nominal pore size no more than 0.22 um) and aseptically filled into pre-sterilised containers; the chosen filter should suit the product and match the filter registered in the marketing authorisation.
system_implications: Filter scan at installation is checked against the product's MA-registered filter make/type/pore rating; any other part number is refused; filter lot, serial and sterilisation evidence (in-house load or supplier gamma certificate) are recorded.
verification_test: Scan a 0.45 um or non-registered filter part number for final filtration; confirm refusal.

requirement: Several filtration points (bioburden-reduction prefilters or additional sterilising-grade filters) may be used upstream; a second sterile sterilising-grade filter close to the point of fill should be considered in the CCS; the filter train is justified against product CQAs (fibres, particles, impurities, adsorption, extractables); the system operates within validated parameters, keeps the filtrate sterile, minimises aseptic connections after the final filter, allows cleaning/SIP and permits in-place integrity testing of the final filter before and after filtration, preferably closed.
system_implications: Filter train is master data (position, role: prefilter / primary sterilising / redundant, required tests per position); the eBMR generates the corresponding install, test and sampling steps from it and counts aseptic connections downstream of the final filter for review.
verification_test: Configure a train with a redundant filter; confirm the batch record generates tests for both positions according to the redundancy logic.

requirement: Sterile filtration is validated per pharmacopoeia under worst case (grouping justified), with bacterial retention using the product or a justified surrogate and justified challenge organism; validation establishes the integrity-test wetting fluid and specification (with precautions if a non-product fluid is used in situ) and process conditions: pre-filtration hold and bioburden effect, conditioning, maximum filtration/contact time, maximum pressure, flow rate, maximum volume, temperature, and time to filter a known volume with its differential pressure.
system_implications: Product/filter master data store each validated parameter with limits (max contact time, max pressure, flow range, max volume, temperature range, integrity-test spec per wetting fluid) and the validation report reference; batch execution compares actual values to them.
verification_test: Enter a filtration volume above the validated maximum; confirm the step is flagged and a deviation is required.

requirement: Routine controls ensure filtration stays within validated parameters; critical parameter results are included in the batch record, including at least the minimum time to filter a known volume and the differential pressure across the filter; significant differences are documented and investigated.
system_implications: Filtration step captures start/end time, volume, flow, upstream/downstream pressure (DP), temperature, and computes filtration time per known volume automatically (from instrument data where available); values outside validated ranges auto-raise a deviation.
verification_test: Import filtration data with a DP above validated maximum; confirm automatic deviation.

requirement: The sterilised filter assembly is integrity tested before use and after sterilisation (PUPSIT) to detect damage from preparation. Where PUPSIT is not feasible (e.g. very small volumes), an alternative is allowed only after a thorough risk assessment and mitigating controls covering filter sterilisation process control, supply chain (contract steriliser, transport, protective packaging) and product/process knowledge (particle burden that could mask a non-integral filter in post-use testing, upstream clarification).
system_implications: PUPSIT is a mandatory step between filter sterilisation and product filtration; it can be omitted only if the product/filter configuration carries an approved PUPSIT-waiver risk assessment reference, which is displayed in the batch record and QP review.
verification_test: Start filtration without PUPSIT on a product with no waiver; confirm block. With an approved waiver, confirm the step is skipped and the waiver ID appears on the batch report.

requirement: Every sterilising-grade filter used on a fluid undergoes a validated, non-destructive integrity test after use and before removal from its housing; the test correlates with bacterial retention (e.g. bubble point, diffusive flow, water intrusion, pressure hold).
system_implications: Post-use integrity test is mandatory before the filter can be recorded as removed; the record holds test type, instrument ID/calibration, wetting fluid, temperature, result vs specification and raw printout/electronic file; a failure blocks certification and opens an investigation.
verification_test: Record filter removal before the post-use test; confirm the system refuses; record a failed post-use test and confirm deviation plus certification block.

requirement: Critical sterile gas and air vent filters linked directly to product sterility are integrity-tested after use while still in their housing; non-critical vent filters are confirmed integral at defined intervals; long-duration gas filters are tested at installation and before replacement, with a risk-based maximum duration of use (uses, sterilisation cycles) specified and monitored; gas filters should not become wet.
system_implications: Filter lifecycle record per serial: role (critical/non-critical), install date, use count, SIP/autoclave cycle count, maximum allowed; critical vent filters get a post-use test step per batch; the system blocks use beyond maximum duration or cycles.
verification_test: Use a tank vent filter beyond its configured maximum SIP cycles; confirm block; complete a batch without the critical vent filter post-use test; confirm certification block.

requirement: If sterility was validated for a multi-filter system, all filters in it should pass post-use integrity testing. In a redundant set-up (second filter as backup only), the primary is tested post-use; if it passes, testing the backup is unnecessary; if it fails, the backup is tested post-use and an investigation and risk assessment determine why the primary failed.
system_implications: Filter-test logic engine: for 'serial validated' trains require post-use pass on all filters; for 'redundant' trains require primary post-use; on primary failure, automatically require redundant post-use test, open an investigation and risk assessment, and show both results at QP review.
verification_test: Record primary post-use fail in a redundant train; confirm the redundant test step appears, an investigation is created, and the batch is blocked until both are complete.

requirement: Bioburden samples are taken from the bulk immediately before the final sterile filtration (before the first filter in a redundant set-up), using sampling systems that do not introduce contamination.
system_implications: A pre-filtration bioburden sampling step with timestamp is mandatory and must precede filtration start; sample ID links to LIMS; the result is compared with the bioburden limit and is a release prerequisite.
verification_test: Record bioburden sampling after filtration started; confirm the sequence violation is flagged; release with bioburden result pending; confirm block.

requirement: Liquid sterilising-grade filters are discarded after one batch and not kept in continuous use beyond one working day unless validated; for CCS-justified, validated campaign use, risks of the duration are assessed, the maximum validated duration documented and enforced with records, and contaminated or defective filters removed.
system_implications: A filter serial can be bound to only one batch (unless the product is configured for validated campaign use); the system times continuous use and blocks beyond one working day or the validated campaign maximum; defective/contaminated flags retire the filter.
verification_test: Scan a filter serial already used in a previous batch; confirm refusal; run a filter past the configured working-day limit without campaign validation; confirm block.

requirement: FFS machines meet the environment rules for terminally sterilised (8.3/8.4) or aseptic (8.10) manufacture as applicable; packaging films are controlled against defined specifications (thickness, strength, microbial and particulate contamination, integrity, artwork) with film bioburden/endotoxin sampling defined in the PQS and CCS.
system_implications: Film roll scan at loading checks lot release against film specification, including bioburden/endotoxin where defined; the FFS line's grade requirement follows the product's sterilisation route.
verification_test: Load a film roll with bioburden result pending; confirm block.

requirement: FFS set-up, filling, sealing and cutting are understood so CPPs are validated, controlled and monitored; product-contact gases (inflation, overlay) are filtered close to point of use and periodically verified; CCS-aligned controls cover critical-zone boundaries, machine and background EM, gowning, integrity testing of filling lines and filters, batch/campaign duration, film decontamination/sterilisation, CIP/SIP, and machine settings and alarm management.
system_implications: FFS master record includes campaign duration limit, CIP/SIP cycle records, gas filter IDs/tests, film decontamination records and imports machine setting changes and alarms into the batch audit trail.
verification_test: Change a sealing set point on the FFS HMI during the batch; confirm the change appears in the batch record with user and time and requires justification if outside validated range.

requirement: FFS critical parameters set in qualification include package dimensions/cutting, forming temperatures (incl. pre-heat and cooling), times and pressures, sealing temperature and its uniformity, sealing time and pressure, environmental and product temperature, batch-specific seal strength and uniformity tests, fill volume/speed/uniformity, printing/embossing settings that protect integrity, and filled-container integrity test methods; they are verified, monitored and recorded during production.
system_implications: FFS execution captures these CPPs continuously or at defined intervals against validated ranges, requires batch-specific seal strength/uniformity test results, and links the CCI results (100 percent for fusion-sealed up to 100 ml).
verification_test: Omit the batch seal-strength test; confirm the batch cannot be closed; import a sealing temperature out of range and confirm affected units are segregated.

requirement: FFS procedures describe detecting and fixing forming/sealing problems; rejected units and sealing issues are recorded and investigated; risk-based maintenance includes inspection plans for seal-critical tooling, with quality-relevant findings documented and investigated.
system_implications: Reject counts by reason (forming, sealing, cutting) are recorded and included in reconciliation; sealing-issue events open investigations; tooling inspection status is checked at line start.
verification_test: Record 50 seal rejects; confirm an investigation is required per configured threshold and that rejects appear in the unit reconciliation.

requirement: BFS for terminally sterilised products is installed in at least Grade D with point-of-fill conditions per 8.3/8.4. For aseptic BFS: shuttle machines need Grade A at the critical zones of parison extrusion, blow-moulding and sealing and a Grade A filling environment at rest and in operation; rotary machines need Grade A inside the parison; the machine sits in at least Grade C provided operators wear Grade A/B clothing, with risk-based personnel monitoring.
system_implications: BFS line master data records machine type (shuttle/rotary) and background grade; gowning checks for BFS operators require Grade A/B garments even in Grade C; personnel monitoring plans are configured per risk for these operators.
verification_test: Attempt to sign on to an aseptic BFS line in Grade C with a Grade C gowning record; confirm refusal.

requirement: In-operation total particle monitoring of BFS critical zones is not expected (design data should show Grade A would be met); viable EM is risk-based per section 9 and covers all critical processing from equipment assembly onward (sampling the rotary critical zone may be impossible); the EM programme accounts for moving parts, complex airflow, heat output, filter configuration and integrity, and cooling system integrity.
system_implications: EM plan engine allows a BFS-specific profile (no in-operation particle counting at the critical zone, with design-data reference) but enforces viable monitoring covering assembly through end of filling; EM coverage gaps in that window are flagged.
verification_test: End viable monitoring 30 minutes before the end of BFS filling; confirm the coverage gap is flagged in batch review.

requirement: BFS air/gases touching critical container surfaces during extrusion, forming or sealing are filtered and periodically verified; polymer granulate storage, sampling and distribution prevent particulate/microbial contamination; the extrusion system's sterility-assurance capability is validated and raw polymer bioburden/endotoxin sampling is defined in the PQS and CCS.
system_implications: Polymer lot issue checks release status incl. bioburden/endotoxin where specified; parison/support-air filter IDs and integrity status are linked to the batch.
verification_test: Charge a polymer lot whose bioburden result is outstanding; confirm block.

requirement: BFS interventions that require stopping filling and/or extrusion, moulding and sealing, and any required re-sterilisation of the filling machine, are specified in the filling SOP and simulated in the APS where relevant.
system_implications: BFS intervention catalogue entries carry flags 'stops extrusion/filling' and 'requires re-sterilisation'; recording such an intervention forces the SIP step and its successful cycle record before filling may resume.
verification_test: Record an intervention flagged 'requires re-sterilisation'; confirm resumption is blocked until a passing SIP record is linked.

requirement: BFS controls align with the CCS (critical zone, EM, gowning, integrity of filling lines/filters, batch/campaign duration, polymer and extrusion temperature control, CIP/SIP, settings and alarms); BFS CPPs include CIP/SIP of product lines and mandrels, extrusion temperature/speed/throat settings (parison thickness), mould temperatures and cooling rate, preparation/sterilisation of added components, EM and cleaning of critical zones, batch-specific wall-thickness tests, fill volumes/speeds/uniformity, printing/embossing settings, 100 percent CCI methods and parameters, and flash-removal cutter settings; they are verified, monitored and recorded in production.
system_implications: BFS batch record captures CIP/SIP cycle IDs, extrusion and mould parameters (continuous import with limits), wall-thickness test results, fill-weight checks, campaign duration timer, and 100 percent CCI counts; out-of-range parameters segregate affected units by time window.
verification_test: Import a mould temperature excursion for 10 minutes; confirm units produced in that window are identified for segregation and assessment.

requirement: BFS blowing/forming/sealing issues are detected and fixed per procedure with rejects and sealing issues recorded and investigated; added components (e.g. LVP caps) are decontaminated and added by a clean controlled process (aseptic: in Grade A using pre-sterilised components; terminal: validation covers all product pathways including unwetted areas) with validated sealing tests; maintenance covers sealing/integrity/sterility-critical items; moulds are critical equipment and any change triggers a container-integrity assessment and, if indicated, validation.
system_implications: eBMR records mould set ID per batch and blocks use of a mould whose change/modification lacks a completed CCI assessment; cap lots require sterilisation evidence for aseptic BFS; rejects by reason feed reconciliation.
verification_test: Install a modified mould without closed CCI assessment; confirm batch start is blocked.

requirement: Lyophilisation is a critical step: every activity that could affect sterility of the product or material is to be treated as an extension of aseptic processing of the sterilised product (the Annex uses 'need to', not 'should'). The accompanying design expectation, preventing contamination from filling to the end of lyophilisation with CCS-defined controls, is a 'should'.
system_implications: Lyo loading, cycle and unloading are aseptic steps in the eBMR: they inherit Grade A checks, operator aseptic qualification checks, intervention logging and EM linkage until the containers are fully sealed.
verification_test: Confirm the lyo loading step requires aseptic-qualified operators and is included in the batch EM coverage window.

requirement: Sterilisation of the lyophiliser and associated items (trays, vial support rings) is validated; the hold time between sterilisation and use is challenged in the APS; the lyophiliser is sterilised regularly per design and re-sterilised after maintenance or cleaning; sterilised equipment is protected afterwards.
system_implications: Lyo readiness check requires a passing SIP record whose age at loading does not exceed the hold time challenged in the latest successful APS, and no maintenance or cleaning event after it; trays/rings require their own sterilisation load IDs.
verification_test: Log a maintenance work order on the lyophiliser after its last SIP; confirm loading is blocked until a new SIP is recorded.

requirement: Lyophilisers and their transfer/loading/unloading areas minimise operator intervention; sterilisation frequency is based on design and contamination risk; lyophilisers loaded or unloaded manually without barrier separation are sterilised before each load; for automated loading/unloading or closed-barrier protection, the frequency is justified and documented in the CCS.
system_implications: Lyophiliser master data holds loading mode (manual-open / automated / closed barrier); for manual-open units the eBMR requires a new successful SIP between every unload and the next load; for others it enforces the CCS-justified interval with the CCS reference displayed.
verification_test: On a manual-open lyophiliser, attempt a second load after unloading without a new SIP; confirm hard block.

requirement: Lyophiliser integrity is maintained after sterilisation and during the cycle; the filter that maintains integrity is sterilised before each use and its integrity test results form part of batch certification; the chamber vacuum/leak test frequency is documented and the maximum permitted air leak rate is specified, with a check at the start of each cycle.
system_implications: Each lyo cycle record must include the start-of-cycle leak-rate result vs specified maximum (fail blocks the cycle) and the vent/breather filter ID, its sterilisation record and its integrity test result, which appears on the QP release checklist.
verification_test: Import a cycle whose start leak rate exceeds the maximum; confirm the cycle is flagged and release blocked; omit the vent filter integrity result and confirm certification block.

requirement: Lyophilisation trays are checked regularly for distortion or damage.
system_implications: Tray IDs are tracked with last inspection date; the loading step refuses trays overdue for inspection or marked damaged.
verification_test: Scan a tray flagged 'misshapen'; confirm refusal.

requirement: Loading/unloading design specifies and documents the loading pattern; partially closed containers move to the lyophiliser under Grade A at all times with minimal direct intervention (conveyors, clean-air transfer carts, portable UDAF) or in validated closed trays/boxes closed in Grade A and not opened in Grade B; transport and venting should not disturb airflow; unsealed containers stay in Grade A, normally separated from operators by barriers; if stoppers are not fully seated before opening the chamber, product stays in Grade A afterwards; loading/unloading utensils are sterile.
system_implications: Lyo loading record captures the shelf-by-shelf loading pattern (tray IDs, vial counts per shelf), transfer method and cart/UDAF ID with its Grade A status during transfer, transfer start/end times, sterile utensil IDs, and at unloading a stopper-seating check; unseated stoppers route units to Grade A handling until capping.
verification_test: Record a transfer with a clean-air cart whose airflow alarm occurred in transit; confirm the affected trays are flagged for assessment.

requirement: Closed systems are designed to reduce manual manipulations; product-contact surface sterility of aseptic closed systems is critical (see AN1-200); connections to the sterile pathway after the final filter are designed to be made aseptically (e.g. intrinsic sterile connectors); the integrity of connection components is assured as defined in the CCS, system integrity tests are considered where sterility could be compromised, and supplier assessment covers failure modes.
system_implications: Closed-system assemblies are recorded as configured items (connectors, tubing, bags) with lot and sterilisation evidence; a configurable pre-use system integrity (pressure decay) test step is available and required when the CCS says so.
verification_test: Configure a closed assembly requiring pre-use pressure-decay testing; skip it and confirm product transfer is blocked.

requirement: A closed system's background grade depends on its design and process: for aseptic processing where integrity could be compromised it is located in Grade A; a lower grade is acceptable only if integrity is shown at every use (e.g. pressure testing/monitoring); transfers between classified areas are assessed; if opened (e.g. maintenance) this happens in a suitable classified area (Grade C for terminal, Grade A for aseptic) or is followed by extra cleaning, disinfection and (aseptic) sterilisation.
system_implications: If a closed system is used outside Grade A for aseptic work, an integrity result must be recorded at every use; a 'system opened' event forces the corresponding cleaning/disinfection/sterilisation steps or a Grade A location for the opening.
verification_test: Use a closed aseptic system in Grade C without an integrity test entry for this use; confirm block.

requirement: SUS are designed to reduce manipulations and manual complexity; CCS assesses SUS-specific risks: product-surface interaction (adsorption, extractables/leachables), fragility, more manual operations and connections, assembly complexity, pre/post-use filter integrity testing, holes and leaks, compromise when opening outer packaging, and particle contamination.
system_implications: SUS installation steps prompt a structured visual inspection (damage, holes, kinks, clamp positions) at unpacking and after installation, record the packaging-opening method, and link the filter-integrity building block for integrated filters.
verification_test: Record a SUS with a detected pinhole at inspection; confirm the assembly is rejected and replaced with traceability of both lots.

requirement: SUS sterilisation is validated without harming performance; supplier assessment (including sterilisation) is critical; for sterile SUS, sterility assurance is verified when qualifying the supplier, and each delivered unit's sterilisation evidence is checked at goods receipt.
system_implications: Goods receipt of sterile SUS requires the sterilisation evidence (irradiation certificate/lot, dose, indicator status) per delivered lot/unit and approved-supplier status; unverified lots cannot be issued to a batch.
verification_test: Receive a SUS lot with no irradiation certificate; confirm the lot stays in quarantine and cannot be scanned into a batch.

requirement: Adsorption and reactivity of product with contact surfaces are evaluated under process conditions; SUS extractable and leachable profiles and their quality impact are evaluated per component, with leachable studies for high-risk components (absorbing materials, long contact times) and realistic, scientifically based simulated conditions.
system_implications: Product-contact material master data carry E&L/adsorption assessment status per product; the eBMR blocks using a SUS component part number for a product for which no assessment is recorded, and enforces any validated maximum contact time.
verification_test: Select a bag part number not assessed for the product; confirm refusal; exceed the validated product-contact time; confirm deviation.

requirement: SUS keep integrity under intended conditions including freeze/thaw and transport (intrinsic sterile connectors, heat- or mechanically sealed, verified to stay integral); risk-based acceptance criteria apply; on receipt each piece is checked against the approved specification and, before use, the outer packaging, label printing and attached documents (certificate of conformance, proof of sterilisation) are visually inspected and the check documented.
system_implications: Pre-use SUS verification step per piece: part number vs approved spec/BOM, outer packaging and pouch condition, label check, CoC and sterilisation proof present; freeze/thaw use requires the SUS to be qualified for that condition.
verification_test: Scan a bag assembly whose part number differs from the approved BOM revision; confirm refusal; skip the documented packaging check and confirm installation cannot be completed.

requirement: Critical manual SUS handling such as assembly and connections is controlled and verified in the APS.
system_implications: SUS assembly/connection steps are tagged as APS-relevant; the operator performing them must be covered by a successful APS that included this manipulation for the line.
verification_test: Assign an operator whose APS participation did not include SUS connections; confirm sign-off is blocked or requires supervision.

requirement: The environmental and process monitoring programme (total particles, viable EM and personnel monitoring, temperature/RH and other characteristics, and APS for aseptic products) is part of the CCS; no element alone proves asepsis; its data are used for routine batch certification/release (for both aseptic and terminally sterilised products) and for periodic review and investigations.
system_implications: The batch release package must automatically assemble EM (viable and total particle), personnel monitoring, room T/RH and DP, and current APS status for every room/line used and the full processing window; the QP cannot certify until all results are final and reviewed.
verification_test: Attempt certification while two settle plates from the filling window are still incubating; confirm block.

requirement: A documented, risk-assessed EM programme defines sampling locations, frequency, methods and incubation conditions, identifies critical monitoring locations (Grade A, aseptic processing areas and Grade B zones interfacing with Grade A) using process, facility, data, flora and airflow-study knowledge, and is reviewed regularly against trends and the CCS.
system_implications: The EM sampling plan attached to each batch is generated from the approved EM programme version (locations, methods, frequency per activity); critical locations are flagged so their results carry higher weight in batch review.
verification_test: Check that a batch shows the EM programme version and that critical locations are visually distinguished in the EM summary.

requirement: Cleanrooms, clean-air devices and personnel are routinely monitored in operation throughout all critical stages, including equipment set-up; for Grade A, particle counting spans all critical processing, equipment assembly included.
system_implications: The eBMR compares the monitoring coverage (particle counter run times, settle-plate exposure windows, active air samples) with the batch's critical processing window from set-up start to end of filling/sealing and flags any gap.
verification_test: Start the Grade A particle counter 20 minutes after aseptic assembly began; confirm a coverage-gap exception.

requirement: Temperature and relative humidity are controlled within ranges suited to product, process and personnel and supporting the cleanliness grade; Grade A monitoring shows aseptic conditions during critical operations at the highest-risk locations with justified device positions; sampling should not contaminate operations.
system_implications: Room T/RH trends for the batch window are attached with limit checks; EM sampling activities inside Grade A are recorded as inherent interventions with time and operator.
verification_test: Replay an RH excursion in the filling room; confirm the batch shows the excursion; confirm Grade A plate changes appear in the intervention log.

requirement: Alert levels and action limits are set for viable and total particle results; action limits are at most the Table 5 (particles) and Table 6 (viable) values and may be tighter from trends, process nature or CCS; alert levels come from qualification data and are periodically reviewed; alert levels are set for Grade A (total particles only), B, C and D to detect adverse trends; Grade C/D in-operation limits come from qualification and routine data.
system_implications: Per-location limit configuration validates action limits against the Annex 1 maxima (locked table) and requires alert levels (except Grade A viable, where any growth is an action event); limit changes are versioned and the version in force is stored with each result.
verification_test: Configure a Grade B active-air action limit of 15 CFU/m3; confirm rejection; confirm a Grade A viable alert level field is not offered.

requirement: Procedures define trending, covering at least rising numbers of alert/action excursions, consecutive alert excursions, recurring isolated action excursions with a possible common cause (e.g. after planned maintenance), and changes in flora type, counts and predominance, with attention to organisms signalling loss of control or hard to eradicate (spore-formers, moulds).
system_implications: EM data model stores organism identification per isolate and event context (e.g. post-maintenance) so configurable trend rules can run; a triggered trend rule creates a linked event visible on all batches in the affected period and area.
verification_test: Enter three consecutive alert excursions at one Grade B location; confirm the trend rule fires and the event is linked to concurrent batches.

requirement: Action-limit excursions require a root-cause investigation, a product impact assessment that includes batches made between sampling and reporting, and CAPA; alert excursions require assessment and follow-up, considering investigation and/or corrective action.
system_implications: When an EM/PM action result is entered, the eBMR automatically links it to every batch processed in that room/zone from the sampling time until the result was reported, places those batches on hold for disposition and opens an investigation with CAPA fields; alert results create an assessment task.
verification_test: Enter an action result on day 5 for a sample taken on day 1; confirm batches processed in that area on days 1-5 are all linked and held.

name: EM routine monitoring - max total particles per m3 (Table 5)
values: Grade A: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 3520; >=5um at rest 29 / in operation 29. Grade B: >=0.5um at rest 3520 / in operation 352000; >=5um at rest 29 / in operation 2930. Grade C: >=0.5um at rest 352000 / in operation 3520000; >=5um at rest 2930 / in operation 29300. Grade D: >=0.5um at rest 3520000 / in operation not predetermined; >=5um at rest 29300 / in operation not predetermined (site sets from risk assessment and routine data). At-rest values to be met after the qualified clean-up period (guidance < 20 min, unmanned). Grade A continuous monitoring sample flow at least 28 L/min (1 ft3/min).

requirement: Occasional isolated 5 um (macro) particle counts in Grade A may be false counts (electronic noise, stray light, coincidence loss), but consecutive or regular low-level counts may signal contamination (filter failure, equipment failure, poor set-up or operating practice) and are investigated.
system_implications: Particle data import applies a rule for Grade A 5 um counts: isolated single counts are annotated, while consecutive or recurring low-level counts within a configurable window raise an event requiring investigation linked to the batch.
verification_test: Replay three consecutive samples each with 1-2 counts at 5 um in Grade A; confirm an investigation event is raised.

requirement: Grade A is monitored continuously for particles of at least 0.5 and 5 um at a sample flow of at least 28 L/min so that interventions, transient events and deterioration are captured; each result is compared frequently with alert/action levels so excursions are found and handled promptly; alarms sound at alert level; procedures define responses including extra microbial monitoring.
system_implications: The eBMR ingests the continuous Grade A particle stream (both size channels) aligned to the batch timeline; alarms appear in context with interventions; an alarm requires a recorded response, and the procedure-driven option to add microbial samples is prompted.
verification_test: Replay an alert-level burst coincident with a corrective intervention; confirm both appear together on the batch timeline and the alarm requires a documented response.

requirement: A similar system is recommended for Grade B, possibly at lower sampling frequency, but frequent and large enough to capture increased contamination and deterioration, with alarms on alert-level exceedance.
system_implications: Grade B particle monitoring (continuous or frequent sequential) is imported for the batch window with alert-level alarms and response records.
verification_test: Replay a Grade B alert exceedance; confirm alarm and response record in the batch.

requirement: Monitoring system choice considers hazards from materials (live organisms, powders, radiopharmaceuticals); where contaminants could damage counters or pose hazards, the strategy assures classification before and after exposure, with increased viable monitoring and periodic monitoring during simulated operations as defined in the CCS; automated monitoring sample volumes are justified.
system_implications: Product master flag 'hazardous material (bio/powder/radio)' switches the batch EM plan to the pre/post-exposure particle strategy with enhanced viable sampling and schedules simulated-operation monitoring.
verification_test: Flag a radiopharmaceutical product; confirm the generated EM plan includes pre- and post-exposure particle checks and extra viable samples.

requirement: During aseptic operations, microbial monitoring is frequent and combines methods (settle plates, volumetric air, glove, gown, surface swabs/contact plates) justified in the CCS without disturbing Grade A/B airflow; room and equipment surfaces are monitored at the end of an operation.
system_implications: Batch EM plan includes each method per location and a mandatory end-of-operation surface sampling step (equipment and room surfaces) before line clearance can be signed.
verification_test: Try to sign line clearance without end-of-operation surface samples; confirm block.

requirement: Viable monitoring is also done when normal manufacturing is not running (after disinfection, before start, at batch completion, after shutdowns) and in associated unused rooms to detect contamination incidents; additional locations can verify the effectiveness of corrective actions after an incident.
system_implications: Line/room readiness shows the status of pre-start and post-disinfection/post-shutdown viable samples; after a shutdown the eBMR requires the post-shutdown monitoring to be taken before batch start, and results are linked to the next batch.
verification_test: Restart a room after a 5-day shutdown; confirm pre-start viable samples are required and linked to the next batch.

requirement: Grade A viable air monitoring (air sampling or settle plates) is continuous for the full critical processing duration including aseptic set-up; a similar approach is considered for Grade B based on risk; monitoring captures interventions, transients and deterioration without adding intervention risk.
system_implications: Settle-plate/air-sampler exposure windows are recorded per Grade A location with start/stop times (max 4 h per plate); the system checks contiguous coverage from set-up start to end of filling and flags gaps or plates exposed more than 4 h.
verification_test: Record a Grade A settle plate exposed 4 h 20 min; confirm it is flagged; leave a 15-minute gap between plates; confirm a coverage gap exception.

requirement: Personnel monitoring locations, types and frequencies are risk-assessed by activity and proximity to critical zones, with periodic in-process sampling; after critical interventions at least gloves (and gown areas if relevant) are sampled; gloves and gown are sampled at each exit from Grade B; after glove sampling following a critical intervention the outer gloves are replaced before continuing, and after gown sampling the gown is replaced before further cleanroom activity.
system_implications: When a corrective (critical) intervention is closed, the eBMR prompts glove-print sampling for each involved operator and then requires an outer-glove change record before the operator's next action; gown sampling after an intervention forces a re-gowning record; every Grade B exit requires glove and gown sample IDs.
verification_test: Close a corrective intervention, take glove prints, and attempt the next step without recording a glove change; confirm block. Exit Grade B without samples; confirm the exit record cannot be completed.

requirement: Personnel in Grade A and B are microbiologically monitored, with extra emphasis on gown monitoring for manual operations (e.g. manual compounding or filling) justified in the CCS; where manufacturing staff perform monitoring, the quality unit oversees it regularly.
system_implications: Manual-process products increase the gown-sampling plan per CCS profile; EM samples record the sampler's identity and role, and a QA oversight record frequency is tracked where production staff sample.
verification_test: Confirm that a manual aseptic compounding batch plan includes gown sampling for every participating operator.

requirement: Rapid/alternative microbial methods should be considered and may be adopted once validated as equivalent or better; sampling methods and equipment are understood, with procedures for correct operation and interpretation and recovery-efficiency data.
system_implications: The EM data model supports non-CFU result units from validated rapid methods (with the CFU-correlated limit and justification reference) and records the sampler device and its validation status.
verification_test: Import a rapid-method result in AFU with a configured correlated limit; confirm the limit evaluation and justification reference are shown.

name: Viable particle maximum action limits for routine monitoring (Table 6)
values: Grade A: no growth for all methods (any growth triggers investigation). Grade B: air 10 CFU/m3; settle plate 90mm 5 CFU/4h; contact plate 55mm 5 CFU/plate; glove print (5 fingers, both hands) 5 CFU/glove. Grade C: air 100; settle 50; contact 25; glove print not specified. Grade D: air 200; settle 100; contact 50; glove print not specified. Settle plates in A and B exposed for the whole operation incl. set-up, max 4 h per plate (exposure validated incl. recovery); C and D exposure max 4 h with frequency by QRM; individual plates may be exposed for less than 4 h. Contact limits apply to equipment, room and gown surfaces in A and B; routine gown monitoring not normally required in C and D. Other methods acceptable if they cover the whole critical process; non-CFU methods need justified, CFU-correlated limits.

requirement: In Grade A any microbial growth results in an investigation.
system_implications: Any non-zero Grade A viable result (air, settle, contact, glove) automatically opens an investigation linked to the batch and blocks certification until closed; no alert tier is offered for Grade A viable data.
verification_test: Enter 1 CFU on a Grade A settle plate; confirm automatic investigation and certification block.

requirement: Microorganisms detected in Grade A and B are identified to species level and their potential impact on product quality for each implicated batch and on the state of control is evaluated; identification in Grade C/D is considered for excursions or indicator organisms (spore-formers, moulds) and often enough to know the typical flora.
system_implications: A Grade A/B positive result cannot be closed without a species-level identification and a per-batch impact assessment entry for each linked batch; organism IDs are stored for flora trending.
verification_test: Close a Grade B contact-plate excursion with genus-only ID; confirm refusal; confirm each linked batch requires its own impact statement.

requirement: APS with sterile nutrient media and/or a non-inhibitory surrogate periodically verifies aseptic controls but is not the primary means of validating the aseptic process (which rests on design, PQS adherence, process controls, training and monitoring); media/surrogate mimic risk-relevant product characteristics, with alternative procedures for semi-solids, powders, lyophilised or heat/cold-processed forms; APS should not be used to justify practices with unnecessary contamination risk.
system_implications: The eBMR supports an APS batch type generated from the same master record as the commercial process, substituting media/surrogate lots (with growth-promotion status) for product, so APS execution evidence is structurally comparable with routine batches.
verification_test: Generate an APS batch from a commercial master record; confirm identical step structure with media lot fields and growth-promotion checks replacing product fields.

requirement: APS mimics routine aseptic manufacture as closely as possible, covering every aseptic step from after sterilisation/decontamination of materials to container sealing, extra aseptic steps for non-filterable products, air instead of inert gas unless anaerobic simulation is intended, a surrogate in the same containers for sterile powder additions, and avoidance of piecemeal unit-operation simulations unless justified and fully covering. Lyophilisation APS covers filling, transport, loading, a representative chamber dwell, unloading and sealing at documented worst case, without boiling or freezing the media, and considering air vacuum break, maximum lyophiliser sterilisation-to-use interval, maximum filtration-to-lyophilisation time, and worst-case quantities (most trays, longest open-door loading).
system_implications: APS batch records must capture the worst-case parameters actually challenged (lyo SIP-to-load interval, filtration-to-loading time, number of trays, loading duration, dwell time, gas used) so the eBMR can derive the qualified envelope that routine lyo batches are checked against.
verification_test: Run an APS with 6 h lyo loading; then run a routine batch with 7 h loading; confirm the routine batch is flagged as outside the APS-qualified envelope.

requirement: APS includes the aseptic manipulations and interventions that occur in routine production plus worst cases; inherent and corrective interventions are performed in a manner and frequency similar to routine, and their inclusion and frequency are risk-based.
system_implications: Each intervention executed in an APS is recorded against the catalogue; the catalogue derives each intervention's 'qualified' status and the maximum frequency demonstrated from successful APS runs; routine batches exceeding the APS-demonstrated count per intervention type are flagged.
verification_test: An APS included 3 needle changes; a routine batch records 5; confirm a flag for QA assessment.

requirement: APS planning considers justified worst-case variables (container size, line speed), representative container/closure sizes with bracketing/matrixing when equivalence is justified, maximum hold times for exposed sterile product and equipment, fill volume enough to contact all surfaces and leave headspace for growth and visible turbidity, air replacing inert gas (with occasional anaerobic runs considered), media supporting pharmacopoeial and local isolates, a justified detection method, sufficient duration to challenge process, intervening operators, shift changes and environment, factors of different/extended shifts (e.g. maximum operator time in the cleanroom), idle interruptions (shift changes, vessel recharging, adding equipment), EM as for routine throughout, campaign start and end risks, and justified end-of-campaign APS only as a supplement.
system_implications: Maintain a per-line 'APS-qualified envelope' built from successful APS records (container/closure sizes, max line speed, max duration, max hold times, max operators and per-operator cleanroom time, shift patterns, idle-interruption types, campaign length); routine batch set-up and execution are checked against it and deviations flagged.
verification_test: Configure a routine batch with a container size not covered by any successful APS bracket; confirm batch creation is blocked.

requirement: For sterile active substances, the APS batch is large enough to represent routine operation, simulate worst-case interventions and cover all product-contact surfaces; all simulated materials are microbiologically evaluated and should not compromise recovery.
system_implications: If the edition is used for sterile API, APS batch size and surface coverage are recorded with justification and all simulation material samples link to their microbial results.
verification_test: Create a sterile-API APS without a surface-coverage justification; confirm the APS protocol cannot be approved.

requirement: Initial validation requires at least three consecutive satisfactory APS covering all shifts, repeated after significant changes affecting sterility assurance (HVAC, equipment, process, number of shifts or personnel, major shutdown); periodic APS is normally twice yearly (about every 6 months) for each aseptic process, filling line and shift; each operator takes part in at least one successful APS every year; APS should be considered after the last batch before shutdown, before long inactivity, and before decommissioning or relocation.
system_implications: APS status engine per process x line x shift (last successful APS date, next due at about 6 months, 'initial validation incomplete' until 3 consecutive passes, 'revalidation required' when a linked change is approved) and per operator (successful APS within 12 months); batch scheduling and start are blocked if the line/shift status is not current; operators without current APS cannot sign Grade A/B aseptic steps.
verification_test: Set a line's last successful night-shift APS at 6 months + 3 weeks; confirm night-shift batch start is blocked (or requires QA override per configured grace); set an operator's last APS at 13 months; confirm aseptic sign-off is blocked.

requirement: For manual aseptic operations (e.g. compounding, filling), each container type, closure and equipment train is initially validated with each operator in at least three consecutive successful APS and revalidated with one APS per operator about every 6 months; the APS batch size mimics routine.
system_implications: For processes flagged 'manual aseptic', operator qualification is tracked per container/closure/equipment-train combination: three consecutive passes initially, then one pass per roughly 6 months; the eBMR blocks an operator from a manual aseptic step for a combination not currently qualified.
verification_test: Assign an operator qualified on 10 ml vials to a manual 50 ml vial fill; confirm refusal.

requirement: APS unit numbers should suffice to simulate all representative activities, with the justification in the CCS; typically at least 5,000 to 10,000 units; for batches under 5,000 units the APS should contain at least as many containers as the production batch.
system_implications: APS master data holds the justified minimum unit count; routine batch creation checks that the planned batch size does not exceed the APS unit count where the APS is below 5,000 units (small-batch rule).
verification_test: With a 3,000-unit APS on file, create a 3,500-unit routine batch on the same line; confirm it is flagged as not covered.

requirement: APS units are agitated, swirled or inverted before incubation; all integral units are incubated and evaluated, including cosmetic defects and units passed through non-destructive IPCs.
system_implications: APS incubation step records inversion/swirl confirmation and incubation of every integral unit; cosmetic rejects and IPC-checked units are counted into the incubated population, not the discard population.
verification_test: Try to classify cosmetic-defect APS units as 'not incubated'; confirm refusal.

requirement: APS units may be discarded without incubation only when comparable with routine discards and only if production SOPs clearly state that such units must be removed in the same circumstances (intervention type, line location, exact number); never more units may be removed in an APS intervention than in a production run; set-up or mandatory line-clearance units are typically incubated separately and not necessarily part of the acceptance criteria. (One of the few places the Annex uses 'must'.)
system_implications: The intervention catalogue defines, per intervention type and line location, the exact number of units that must be removed; the same definition drives routine and APS batches; in an APS the eBMR refuses to record more removed units than the catalogue value, and set-up/line-clearance units are tracked as a separately incubated population.
verification_test: In an APS, record removal of 12 units for an intervention whose catalogue value is 8; confirm refusal; confirm the same catalogue value is enforced in a routine batch.

requirement: Discarded materials that contacted product surfaces (e.g. flushes) are simulated with media and incubated unless shown irrelevant to sterility; units are incubated in clear containers (identical-configuration clear substitutes for amber/opaque, else a validated detection method), promptly and under justified, validated conditions; isolates are identified to species where practical; after incubation, trained and qualified personnel inspect units under suitable conditions, and samples receive positive controls with reference organisms and local isolates.
system_implications: APS record captures flush-media units, container substitution details, fill-end to incubation-start time (flag if beyond the defined limit), incubation temperatures/durations, inspector qualification (APS reading), growth promotion results and isolate identifications.
verification_test: Assign an APS reader without the APS-inspection qualification; confirm refusal; enter an incubation start 30 h after fill end with a 24 h limit; confirm a deviation.

requirement: The target is zero growth; any contaminated unit means the APS has failed. Required follow-up: root-cause investigation; corrective measures; normally at least three consecutive successful repeat APS; a prompt review of all aseptic production records since the last successful APS, including a risk assessment of possible sterility breaches in batches made since then; all unreleased batches included in the investigation scope with release decisions considering its outcome; quarantine of all products made on the line after the failure until it is resolved; limits on implicated operators until retrained and requalified; production resumes only after successful revalidation.
system_implications: Recording a positive APS unit sets the APS to FAILED and automatically: (1) places every batch made on that line since the failed APS in quarantine; (2) builds the list of all batches since the last successful APS and requires a per-batch sterility-breach risk assessment, with unreleased batches blocked pending the investigation; (3) sets the line status to 'production suspended' until three consecutive successful repeat APS (configurable) are approved; (4) restricts implicated operators to non-aseptic work until requalified.
verification_test: Enter one turbid unit in an APS; confirm line suspension, automatic quarantine of batches made since the APS, investigation scope listing batches since the prior successful APS, and operator restriction; confirm the line unlocks only after three consecutive passing repeat APS.

requirement: Each APS run is fully documented with a reconciliation of units (filled, incubated, not incubated) and justification for non-incubated units; every intervention is recorded with start and end time and the person involved; all microbial monitoring and other test data go into the APS batch record; an APS is aborted only where written procedures would require the same for commercial lots, and the abort is investigated.
system_implications: APS batch record enforces unit reconciliation (filled = incubated + justified non-incubated + separately incubated set-up units) with zero unexplained difference, the same intervention log as routine batches, embedded EM/PM results, and an 'abort' action available only with the procedure reference that would apply to a commercial lot plus an investigation link.
verification_test: Close an APS with 5 unexplained units; confirm refusal; attempt to abort an APS for a reason not listed as a commercial abort criterion; confirm refusal.

requirement: The initial APS validation is repeated when an aseptic process has not run for an extended period, or after changes to process, equipment, procedures or environment that could affect it, or when new containers or container-closure combinations are added.
system_implications: The APS status engine tracks the last production date per process/line; inactivity beyond the configured period, an approved change tagged 'affects aseptic process', or a new container/closure master record reset the line to 'initial validation required' (three consecutive APS).
verification_test: Add a new stopper type to the line; confirm status changes to 'initial APS validation required' for that configuration and batch creation is blocked.

requirement: Staff trained and experienced in microbiology and sterility assurance support process design, the EM regime and investigations of microbiological events; specifications for raw materials, components and products include microbial, particulate and endotoxin/pyrogen limits where monitoring or the CCS indicates a need.
system_implications: Investigations of microbiological events raised from the eBMR require an approver with a sterility-assurance/microbiology role; material issue checks include micro/endotoxin/particulate spec results when the specification has them.
verification_test: Try to approve a Grade B excursion investigation with a user lacking the microbiology role; confirm refusal.

requirement: Every batch, aseptic or terminally sterilised, has a bioburden assay whose result is considered in final batch review; bioburden limits apply immediately before the final sterilising filter or the terminal sterilisation, linked to the method's efficiency; samples represent worst case (e.g. end of hold time); with overkill terminal cycles, bioburden is monitored at scheduled intervals.
system_implications: The pre-sterilisation bioburden sample step is placed at the worst-case point (end of the hold, just before filtration or loading into the terminal steriliser), is timestamped relative to the hold and filtration/sterilisation start, and its result against the product limit is a mandatory release item (scheduled-interval option for overkill terminal products).
verification_test: Take the bioburden sample at the start of a 12 h hold instead of the end; confirm the step warns that the sample point is not the configured worst case; release with result missing; confirm block.

requirement: For products with parametric release, a pre-sterilisation bioburden programme on filled units is in place with an assay each batch, worst-case representative sampling locations, identification of organisms found and assessment of their effect on the sterilising process, and endotoxin monitoring where appropriate.
system_implications: Parametric-release products require per-batch filled-unit bioburden samples from configured worst-case positions before the cycle starts, with organism identification and a sterilisation-resistance assessment required for any recovery.
verification_test: Record a bioburden recovery on a parametric-release batch without organism ID; confirm release is blocked.

requirement: The finished-product sterility test is only the last of a series of critical controls; a pass cannot rescue a batch that failed its design, procedural or validation requirements; the test method is validated for each product.
system_implications: Release logic: a passing sterility test never clears an open process, validation or procedural nonconformance; certification requires both a valid sterility result (validated method for this product) and closure of all process exceptions.
verification_test: With a passing sterility test and an open sterilisation-cycle deviation, attempt certification; confirm block.

requirement: Sterility testing is done aseptically on samples representative of the whole batch but including those most at risk: for aseptic fills, containers from the beginning and end of the batch plus, based on risk, after critical interventions; for products heat-sterilised in final containers, worst-case load positions (coolest/slowest to heat) of each load; for lyophilised products, samples from different lyophiliser loads; where sub-batches exist (e.g. separate autoclave loads) each sub-batch is sampled and tested separately, with separate testing considered for other tests.
system_implications: The eBMR generates the sterility sampling plan automatically: start and end of fill (by unit counter/time), after each recorded critical intervention (risk rule), cold-spot positions per terminal-sterilisation load (each load = sub-batch with own sample set and test), and per lyophiliser load; each sample keeps its origin (time, position, load) through to LIMS.
verification_test: Run a terminally sterilised batch across 3 autoclave loads; confirm 3 sub-batch sterility sample sets from cold-spot positions are required; record a corrective intervention in an aseptic fill; confirm an extra sterility sample is prompted per the risk rule.

requirement: Where shelf life is too short to await the sterility result (or EM results at manufacture), process design, extra monitoring and/or alternative test methods mitigating the risks are assessed and documented; EM compliance then includes review of the most recent available data, and rapid methods should be considered.
system_implications: Products flagged 'short shelf life' use a release path that allows certification before sterility/EM results, provided a documented risk mitigation is referenced and the most recent available EM data are reviewed; late results remain linked to the batch with automatic escalation (recall assessment) if adverse.
verification_test: Certify a short-shelf-life batch before the sterility result; later enter a positive sterility result; confirm automatic escalation linked to the distributed batch.

requirement: Decontamination of sterility-sample exteriors (e.g. VHP, UV) should not reduce test sensitivity or sample reliability; product-test media are QC-tested per pharmacopoeia before use; EM and APS media are growth-promotion tested before use with justified reference organisms and representative local isolates, normally by the end user (reliance on supplier/outsourced testing justified, with transport considered); rapid/automated methods are validated for the product or process.
system_implications: At EM/APS plate or media issue, the scanned media lot must have a passing growth-promotion record (end-user or justified supplier reliance); plates from non-released lots cannot be linked to batch samples.
verification_test: Scan a settle-plate lot without GPT release at the Grade A station; confirm refusal.

requirement: EM data and trend data for the classified areas are reviewed as part of batch certification/release, with a written procedure defining actions for out-of-trend results or limit excursions.
system_implications: The QP/QA review screen shows, for all rooms/zones used by the batch and the whole processing window, EM results versus alert/action limits and the current trend status (with any trend-rule triggers), and requires an explicit reviewed/accepted signature before certification.
verification_test: Confirm the release checklist cannot be completed without the EM/trend review signature; confirm an open out-of-trend event is shown and blocks certification until dispositioned.

clause: Glossary: Inherent / Corrective / Critical intervention; Critical zone; Critical surfaces
requirement: Interventions are classified two ways: inherent (integral to set-up, routine operation or monitoring and required by procedure, e.g. aseptic assembly, container replenishment, EM sampling) versus corrective (made to correct or adjust the process, not at a set frequency, e.g. clearing jams, stopping leaks, adjusting sensors, replacing parts); an intervention of either type that enters the critical zone (where product and critical surfaces are exposed) is a critical intervention.
system_implications: The intervention data model must carry two independent attributes, type (inherent/corrective) and criticality (critical zone entered yes/no), plus qualified status; rules keyed on 'critical' (glove sampling and change, extra sterility samples, EM alignment) and on 'corrective' (frequency trending vs APS) use these attributes.
verification_test: Record an inherent critical intervention (stopper replenishment into Grade A) and a corrective non-critical one; confirm the post-intervention glove-sampling rule fires only for the critical one.

requirement: Grade A air supply is air through a filter qualified to give Grade A total-particle quality, without a requirement for continuous particle monitoring or Grade A viable limits; it protects fully stoppered, not yet crimped vials.
system_implications: Zone master data must distinguish 'Grade A zone' from 'Grade A air supply' so the EM rule engine does not demand continuous particle monitoring or Grade A viable limits at a clean-process capping station, while still recording its air supply status.
verification_test: Configure the capper as 'Grade A air supply'; confirm the batch EM plan does not require continuous particle counting there but does show air supply status.

clause: Glossary: Operator; Manual aseptic processing; Closed system; Local isolates
requirement: 'Operator' includes anyone in the processing operation (set-up, filling, maintenance and other associated personnel); manual aseptic processing covers hand compounding, filling, placing or sealing of open containers of sterile product; a closed system keeps the product unexposed, is sterilised after connections are made (for sterile products), stays closed until the operation ends and excludes RABS/isolators; local isolates are representative site organisms from Grade A/B EM, personnel monitoring or positive sterility tests.
system_implications: Qualification gates apply to every 'operator' role including maintenance; product/process master flags 'manual aseptic' and 'closed system' use these definitions to select APS rules (9.39) and background-grade rules (8.130); local-isolate library entries come from EM/PM/sterility identifications and are used in GPT and APS positive controls.
verification_test: Confirm a maintenance engineer entering Grade B during a batch is subject to the same gowning/APS gate as filling operators.

name: Glossary numeric definitions relevant to eBMR rules
values: Terminal sterilisation SAL: 1e-6 or better. Post-aseptic terminal heat treatment: shown SAL of 1e-6 or better without meeting steam sterilisation requirements (e.g. F0 of at least 8 min). Overkill sterilisation: at least 12 log10 reduction of organisms with minimum D-value of 1 min. Sterilising-grade filter: usually pore size 0.22 um or less. Bacterial retention test: typically Brevundimonas diminuta at least 1e7 CFU/cm2. Dead leg: non-circulating pipe longer than 3 internal pipe diameters. Isokinetic sampling: inlet velocity within about +/-20 percent of local airflow. D-value: duration/dose for 90 percent reduction; Z-value: temperature change for 10-fold D-value change. Equilibration time: from reference point reaching sterilisation temperature to all load points reaching it.

requirement: Facility and equipment design expectations (smooth impervious surfaces, no hard-to-clean recesses, low-shedding materials, sealed ceilings, no sinks/drains in Grade A/B, trapped drains elsewhere, observation windows/cameras, up-to-date equipment descriptions and P&IDs, utility installation records, no exposed pipework in cleanrooms) are verified through facility qualification, not batch execution.
system_implications: No direct eBMR function; the eBMR relies on the room/equipment qualification status (AN1-031, AN1-034, AN1-042). Traceability entry only, so the requirement matrix is complete.
verification_test: Traceability review: confirm these clauses map to the qualification-status check rather than to execution steps.

requirement: Senior management oversees the state of control; risk-management outcomes are reviewed regularly, during change, for significant emerging problems and in the periodic product quality review; CCS effectiveness forms part of management review; utility, defect and EM data are trended.
system_implications: The eBMR must store execution data in structured, queryable form (interventions by type/count/duration, hold times achieved, defect counts by code, EM links, filter test values, cycle results, deviations) and provide cross-batch exports/dashboards to feed PQR, CCS review and management review.
verification_test: Export 12 months of interventions per line by type and duration; confirm data are complete and match the batch records.

name: Minimum background grade by barrier technology
values: Open isolator: generally at least Grade C (clause 4.20(i)(a)). Closed isolator: at least Grade D. RABS for aseptic processing: at least Grade B. Conventional open aseptic line (Grade A zone): Grade B. Aseptic BFS: machine in at least Grade C with operators in Grade A/B garments. BFS for terminal sterilisation: at least Grade D. Clean-process vial capping under Grade A air supply: background at least Grade D. Terminally sterilised filling: Grade C (Grade A with at least Grade C background when unusually at risk).

name: Personnel and APS frequencies
values: Gowning qualification reassessment: at least annually (visual + microbial: gloved fingers, forearms, chest, hood/mask/forehead). Operator participation in a successful APS: at least once a year. Periodic APS: normally twice a year (about every 6 months) per aseptic process, per filling line, per shift. Initial APS validation: at least 3 consecutive successful runs covering all shifts. After APS failure: normally at least 3 consecutive successful repeat APS. Manual aseptic: each operator 3 consecutive successful APS initially per container/closure/equipment train, then one about every 6 months. APS size: typically at least 5,000-10,000 units; for batches below 5,000 units, at least the production batch size. APS acceptance target: zero growth (any contaminated unit = failure). Visual inspection operator qualification: at least annually incl. eyesight check.

name: Equipment and utility test frequencies and process values
values: Isolator glove integrity test: at least beginning and end of each batch or campaign (session start/end for small manual batches) plus visual check at each use. Steriliser vacuum leak test: periodic, normally weekly. Autoclave air-removal test: normally daily (or air detector). Heat sterilisation revalidation: at least annually for worst-case load patterns. Depyrogenation tunnel HEPA integrity: at least biannually (twice a year). Depyrogenation validation: at least 3 log10 endotoxin reduction with suitable Fh. Liquid sterilising filter: one batch only, not more than one working day continuous use unless validated. Sterilising filter nominal pore size: 0.22 um maximum (also for process gases). Water sampling: at least one representative sample every day of water used in manufacture. WFI storage/circulation example: above 70 C. Particle counter sample tubing: typically no longer than 1 m. Grade A particle sample flow: at least 28 L/min. Lyophiliser leak rate: checked at start of every cycle against specified maximum. Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml (glass ampoules, BFS): 100 percent CCI.

name: Validated maximum time windows the eBMR must enforce (values are product/site-specific; Annex 1 requires them to exist)
values: (1) Cleaning-to-drying-to-sterilisation hold of equipment/components/containers [8.18(i)]. (2) Sterilised equipment/components/containers hold before use and during filling/assembly [8.18(ii); 8.46]. (3) Decontaminated RABS/isolator hold before use [8.18(iii)]. (4) Start of product preparation to sterilisation or sterilising filtration, through to end of aseptic filling, per product [8.18(iv); 8.36]. (5) Sterilised product hold before filling [8.18(v)]. (6) Aseptic processing time [8.18(vi)]. (7) Filling time [8.18(vii)]. (8) Terminal sterilisation products: preparation to filling [8.5]. (9) Packing to sterilisation and sterile shelf life of packed items [8.48]. (10) Post-SIP hold under integrity until use [8.63]. (11) Lyophiliser sterilisation to use, as challenged in APS [8.122; 9.33(vii)]. (12) Filtration contact time / maximum filtration time, pre-filtration hold [8.85]. (13) Sterile gown maximum wear time per shift [7.15]. (14) Settle plate exposure max 4 h [9.30]. (15) Clean-up period after operations, guidance under 20 min [4.29]. (16) Disinfectant dilution in-use expiry [4.34; 4.35]. (17) Filter use duration in validated campaigns [8.95]. (18) EO aeration minimum [8.78]. (19) APS unit incubation start without unnecessary delay [9.44].

name: Minimum gowning by grade (summary)
values: Grade B and entry/interventions into Grade A: dedicated undergarments; sterile gloves while donning; sterile headgear enclosing all hair incl. facial hair (tucked into suit); sterile facemask and sterile eye covers enclosing all facial skin; sterilised footwear/over-boots with trousers tucked in; sleeves tucked into a second pair of sterile gloves; fresh sterilised garments at every entry; max wear time from garment qualification. Grade C: hair/beard covered; one- or two-piece trouser suit gathered at wrists with high neck; disinfected shoes/overshoes. Grade D: hair/beard covered; general protective suit; disinfected shoes/overshoes. Extra gloves/facemask in C/D when the CCS identifies a contamination-risk activity. Facility suit and socks worn before entering B and C change rooms.

name: BB-01 Room, zone and line master data (classification and readiness)
purpose: Single source for where each step may run and whether the location is currently fit for use.
fields: room/zone ID
grade (A/B/C/D/unclassified) and zone type (Grade A zone vs Grade A air supply)
barrier technology (open/closed isolator, open/closed RABS, conventional, BFS shuttle/rotary)
background room and its grade
qualification status and last/next requalification date (A/B 6 months, C/D 12 months)
requalification-required flag after change/remediation
DP pairs, set points, alarm limits (>=10 Pa guidance between grades) and criticality
UDAF velocity range reference (0.36-0.54 m/s guidance)
clean-up period (qualified, <20 min guidance)
maximum operator count (<= APS-qualified number)
cleaning/disinfection status and sporicide due date
airflow visualisation study reference
rules: Block step start if room/zone grade is below the step's required grade or background grade is below the technology minimum
Block if qualification expired or requalification-required flag set
Block if cleaning/disinfection or sporicide overdue
Start clean-up timer after line clearance/disruption and block restart until elapsed
Raise batch event when occupancy exceeds maximum
Grade A air supply zones excluded from continuous particle and Grade A viable rules but air-supply status recorded

name: BB-02 Personnel qualification gate (sign-on, room entry, e-signature)
purpose: Ensure only currently qualified people perform or sign each activity in each grade.
fields: user ID and roles (operator incl. maintenance/cleaning/EM sampler, inspector, QA, QP, microbiologist)
cleanroom and aseptic training status
gowning qualification date and result (visual + microbial), next due (<= 12 months)
APS participation history (line, shift, process, container/closure/equipment train, result, date)
disqualification status and reason (PM trend, failed APS, assessment)
visual inspection qualification + eyesight check date
supervised-entry flag and supervising authorised person
health/tissue-culture exposure declaration
rules: Unsupervised Grade A/B sign-off only with gowning qualified within 12 months AND successful APS within 12 months covering the line/process
Manual aseptic steps require per-operator APS for the specific container/closure/equipment train (3 initial, then ~6-monthly)
Disqualified users blocked from aseptic steps until retraining, gowning requalification and (default) successful APS are linked
Failed APS or PM adverse-trend rule sets disqualification automatically for implicated operators
Unqualified persons may enter only via exceptional supervised-entry record with impact assessment, linked to in-progress batches
Visual inspectors blocked if VI qualification or eyesight check older than 12 months

name: BB-03 Gowning and garment log
purpose: Record each cleanroom entry/exit with garment traceability, checks and wear time.
fields: operator
entry time, exit time, room/grade
garment and eye-cover pack lot IDs, sterilisation lot, sterile expiry
packaging-intact check
pre-donning and post-donning visual checks
garment cycle count (laundry/sterilisation) if tracked
gown wear timer vs qualified maximum
glove disinfection events
glove/garment change events and reason (damage, post-intervention sampling)
exit integrity check
exit glove and gown sample IDs (Grade B)
fitness/exposure declarations
rules: Reject expired, unsterilised or damaged garment packs
Reject garments beyond maximum laundry/sterilisation cycles
Fresh sterile garments required at each Grade A/B entry
Alert at maximum wear time; record as batch event if exceeded
Exit record incomplete until exit integrity check and Grade B exit glove/gown samples recorded
Glove change enforced after post-critical-intervention glove sampling; re-gown enforced after post-intervention gown sampling

name: BB-04 Material and equipment transfer into Grade A/B
purpose: Control and document every item entering or leaving aseptic areas.
fields: item ID/type
approved-transfer-list reference or QA exception ID (risk assessment, disinfection and monitoring plan)
transfer route (double-door autoclave, depyrogenation tunnel, pass-through, airlock, RTP/beta container, bacteria-retentive filter)
sterilisation load/cycle ID where applicable
outer-layer disinfection: agent, lot, expiry, contact time, operator
packaging layers removed at each grade change
time in / time out and direction (in/out) for time-based separation
non-sterilisable item flag with EM location assignment
rules: Unlisted items blocked unless a pre-approved QA exception is linked
Lower-to-higher grade transfers require a disinfection record
Sterile items require a released sterilisation cycle and valid sterile hold
Where time-based separation is used, overlapping in/out movements raise a warning
Non-sterilisable items added to the batch surface-monitoring plan

name: BB-05 Sterilisation load and cycle record (moist heat, dry heat, EO, contract/irradiation)
purpose: Identify every load and prove each cycle conformed before any item from it is used, and present all contributing cycles at release.
fields: unique cycle ID
steriliser ID, qualification status, last leak test (weekly), last air-removal test (daily) or air detector result
validated cycle recipe/version and validated load pattern ID (with min/max load)
load contents: item IDs/carriers, product name, batch number, quantity per item type
