load carrier labels/electronic tracking state (to sterilise / sterilised-pending review / released / rejected)
packing time and packing-to-sterilisation limit
control and independent monitoring probe data (IDs, positions), chamber drain temperature, pressure
equilibration time, exposure time, min/max temperature, P-T saturation check, F0 (fluid loads)
dry heat: temperature, exposure time, chamber overpressure incl. hold, air speed/quality, belt speed/dwell and zone temperatures and DP profile for tunnels, Fh
EO: preconditioning time/temperature/RH, gas concentration, pressure, gas amount, RH, temperature, exposure time, aeration start/end, residuals
BI lot (incoming verification status), BI positions, results, positive control
cooling medium and its sterilisation evidence
unload checks: load dryness, per-item damage/packaging integrity/moisture
cycle outcome (automated evaluation) and reviewer approval
sterile expiry per item
contract sterilisation certificate (dose range, processing lot) for externally sterilised items
rules: Only validated recipe + validated load pattern selectable; item counts checked vs min/max
Block steriliser use if leak test, air-removal test, requalification (annual worst-case) or maintenance release is outstanding
Automatic comparison of every critical parameter and phase duration to validated limits; any failure or deviation (incl. longer/shorter phases) quarantines the load and opens an investigation
Exposure timing valid only after full-load equilibration
BI pass can never override a failed physical parameter
Unload dryness and per-item inspection mandatory; unfit items removed and investigated
Items consumable only in 'released' state and within sterile expiry
All cycle IDs contributing to a batch listed in the release package and each must be approved

name: BB-06 Time-window and hold-time engine
purpose: Enforce every validated maximum time in real time from execution timestamps rather than operator arithmetic.
fields: window type (see limit table of 19 windows)
start event and end event references
validated maximum (and minimum where relevant) with validation reference
product/material/equipment scope
current elapsed time and projected expiry
storage condition during hold
exceedance record and deviation link
rules: Timers start and stop from recorded events (not typed durations)
Pre-expiry warning and hard stop at expiry for sterile holds, prep-to-fill, filtration contact, filling time and aseptic processing time
Expiry mid-operation (e.g. stopper hold during filling) raises an immediate event and requires QA decision
Routine limits cannot exceed the durations challenged in the latest successful APS (holding times, fill duration, lyo sterilisation-to-use)
Exceedances appear in review-by-exception and block certification until dispositioned

name: BB-07 Sterilising filter lifecycle and integrity test record
purpose: Trace every liquid, gas and vent filter and apply the PUPSIT, post-use, redundant and multi-filter logic.
fields: filter serial/lot, part number, pore rating, role (bioburden-reduction prefilter / primary sterilising / redundant / serial-validated train member / critical gas or vent / non-critical vent / lyophiliser integrity filter)
MA-registered filter reference
filter sterilisation evidence (autoclave/SIP cycle ID or supplier irradiation certificate)
installation time, batch ID, first product contact time, removal time
use count and sterilisation-cycle count vs maximum; campaign validation reference
PUPSIT: test type (bubble point, diffusion, water intrusion, pressure hold), wetting fluid, temperature, spec, result, instrument ID and calibration, raw data file
PUPSIT waiver risk-assessment reference (if applicable)
post-use test (before removal from housing): same fields
filtration CPPs: volume, flow, upstream/downstream pressure, DP, temperature, time per known volume, total contact time
pre-filtration bioburden sample ID and time
rules: Part number must match the product's MA-registered filter
Serial bound to one batch; continuous use limited to one working day unless validated campaign (then validated maximum enforced)
PUPSIT mandatory between sterilisation and filtration unless an approved waiver is referenced
Post-use test mandatory before removal is recorded; failure blocks certification and opens investigation
Serial-validated multi-filter train: every filter must pass post-use
Redundant train: primary post-use required; on primary failure, redundant post-use test required plus investigation and risk assessment
Critical gas/vent filters: post-use test in housing per batch; results on release checklist
Non-critical vent filters: interval testing, test at installation and before replacement, maximum duration/cycles enforced
Filtration CPP outside validated range triggers deviation
Bioburden sample must precede filtration start (before first filter in redundant set-up)

name: BB-08 Intervention and stoppage log (with intervention catalogue)
purpose: Capture every intervention and stoppage in a structured way that links to APS qualification, EM, sampling and batch disposition.
fields: catalogue ID or 'non-qualified' flag
type: inherent or corrective
critical-zone entry (critical intervention yes/no)
line/zone/filling position
start and end timestamp (duration computed)
operators involved
units removed (count, positions) vs catalogue-defined removal number
tools used (sterile tool IDs)
concurrent EM/particle data window reference
QA authorisation (for non-qualified)
post-intervention glove/gown samples and glove change
stoppage cause (auto from PLC where available)
APS in which this intervention was qualified, max frequency demonstrated
rules: Selectable interventions limited to catalogue items qualified by a valid successful APS for the line
Non-qualified intervention requires real-time QA authorisation, auto-deviation and mandatory QA assessment at disposition
Units removed must equal the catalogue number for that intervention/location; APS may never remove more than routine
Critical interventions trigger glove sampling then glove change; gown sampling triggers re-gown
Routine counts per intervention type above APS-demonstrated frequency are flagged
Critical interventions can trigger additional sterility samples (risk rule)
Interventions requiring re-sterilisation (e.g. BFS) block resumption until a passing SIP is linked
All interventions and stoppages shown on the batch timeline with particle/EM data

name: BB-09 Environmental monitoring linkage (viable, total particle, DP, T/RH)
purpose: Bind all environmental data for the batch's rooms and processing window to the batch and evaluate coverage, limits and trends.
fields: EM programme version and generated sampling plan per batch
location ID, grade, critical-location flag
method (settle plate, active air, contact, swab, continuous particle 0.5/5 um, rapid method)
media lot and growth-promotion status
exposure start/stop (settle plate max 4 h)
sampler identity and role
result, units (CFU or justified non-CFU), limit version in force (alert/action)
organism identification (species for A/B)
continuous particle stream reference (sample flow >= 28 L/min), counter ID and calibration
DP, temperature and RH trends and alarms with acknowledgement and assessment
pre-start, post-disinfection, post-shutdown and end-of-operation samples
rules: Coverage check: Grade A viable and particle monitoring continuous from aseptic set-up/assembly to end of critical processing; gaps flagged
Action limits validated against Annex 1 Tables 5 and 6 maxima; alert levels required (not for Grade A viable)
Grade A any growth = investigation; A/B isolates identified to species
Action excursion links to all batches in the area from sampling until reporting and holds them
Trend rules (consecutive alerts, rising counts, recurring post-maintenance excursions, spore-formers/moulds, flora shifts, repeated low 5 um counts in Grade A) create batch-linked events
Critical DP alarm during open processing requires documented assessment; alarms cannot be silently overridden
Batch cannot be certified while any sample in the window is pending or any linked excursion is open

name: BB-10 Isolator and RABS readiness and integrity
purpose: Prove the barrier system was intact and decontaminated for the batch and capture events that break separation.
fields: barrier type and ID
glove/sleeve per port: installed date, replacement due (CCS interval), visual check per use
glove integrity/leak test per port at batch or campaign start and end (tester ID, result)
isolator enclosure leak test date
cleaning record preceding bio-decontamination
bio-decontamination cycle ID, recipe, agent lot, parameters vs validated ranges, glove-extension confirmation, result
decontaminated-hold start and expiry
RABS sporicidal disinfection record; RABS glove sterilisation/bio-decontamination per campaign
door opening events (RABS) and glove exposure disinfection records
transfer port (RTP) events
rules: Block aseptic phase if bio-decontamination failed, was not preceded by cleaning or its hold expired
Block batch start if any glove is past replacement date or isolator leak test overdue
Failed end-of-batch glove test raises a deviation covering the period since the last passing test
RABS door opening requires justification, assessment and glove disinfection before next aseptic step
Glove breach during processing is a batch impact event

name: BB-11 APS status and qualified-envelope engine
purpose: Know at any moment whether a line/process/shift and each operator is covered by a valid APS, and what worst-case envelope that APS qualified.
fields: APS ID, line, process, shift(s), container/closure sizes (bracket/matrix), date, result
initial validation counter (3 consecutive passes) and revalidation due (about 6 months)

qualified envelope: max duration, line speed, max hold times, operators and per-operator time in cleanroom, interventions and frequencies, idle interruptions, campaign length, lyo SIP-to-use interval, filtration-to-lyo time, trays and loading duration, gas used
participants per APS and their roles/interventions performed
status: valid / due / initial validation required / suspended after failure
change-control links that require APS (HVAC, equipment, process, shifts, staffing, major shutdown, new container/closure)
last production date per process (inactivity trigger)
rules: Batch creation/start blocked when line/process/shift APS status is not valid
Routine batch parameters outside the qualified envelope flagged or blocked (configurable)
Approved change tagged 'affects aseptic process' or long inactivity sets 'initial validation required'
Failed APS sets status 'suspended': no production until the required consecutive successful repeat APS (normally 3) are approved
Operator APS currency (12 months; manual aseptic ~6 months per combination) feeds BB-02

name: BB-12 APS batch record
purpose: Execute and document a media fill with the same structure as a commercial batch plus APS-specific reconciliation and failure handling.
fields: master record source/version (commercial) and APS protocol
media/surrogate lots with growth-promotion and sterility status; air replacing inert gas unless anaerobic
units filled, units incubated, units not incubated (with SOP-based justification per intervention), set-up/line-clearance units incubated separately, flush-media units
agitation/inversion confirmation
fill end time, incubation start time, incubation conditions and durations
container substitution (clear containers) details
intervention log (as BB-08) with start/end and persons
EM and PM results for the full APS duration
reading inspectors and their qualification; results per unit; positive controls (reference and local isolates)
isolate identification (species where practical)
abort record (procedure reference) and investigation
rules: Reconciliation must balance with zero unexplained units
Units removed per intervention cannot exceed routine catalogue values
All integral units incl. cosmetic rejects and non-destructive IPC units incubated
Any positive unit = failed APS, triggering BB-11 suspension and BB-13 impact scope (all batches since last successful APS; quarantine of all batches since the failed APS; operator restrictions)
Abort only for reasons that would apply to commercial lots, with investigation

name: BB-13 Batch impact assessment and excursion engine
purpose: Turn any Annex 1-relevant event into a scoped, justified impact assessment linked to every potentially affected batch, and hold certification until resolved.
fields: trigger type and source record
affected area/line/equipment/utility and time window
auto-proposed batch scope (by time window and location)
per-batch inclusion/exclusion decision with mandatory rationale
root cause, product risk statement, CAPA link, residual-risk acceptance
microbiology reviewer (for micro events)
market-impact assessment (for trends affecting released product)
disposition recommendation per batch
rules: Triggers include: EM/PM action excursion (scope from sampling to reporting) [9.13]; any Grade A growth [9.30]; adverse EM trend [9.11]; failed APS (all batches since last successful APS; quarantine since failure) [9.46]; non-qualified intervention [8.16]; failed or deviating sterilisation cycle [8.41]; failed PUPSIT/post-use/vent filter test [8.87-8.92; 6.19; 8.124]; filtration CPP deviation [8.86]; glove or barrier integrity failure [4.21]; critical DP alarm/air supply failure [4.16]; unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment [5.7]; water action excursion or post-sanitisation results pending [6.12; 6.14]; hold-time exceedance [8.18]; unusual defect rates or critical defect after 100 percent inspection [8.30]; AVI challenge failure [8.32]; lyo leak-rate failure or loss of integrity [8.124]; unqualified person entry [7.5]; sterility test failure [3.2]
Certification blocked while any linked assessment is open
Inclusion/exclusion rationale mandatory for every candidate batch
Assessment outcomes propagate to all listed batches, including released ones where market impact must be considered

name: BB-14 Lyophilisation record
purpose: Treat the lyophilisation chain as an extension of aseptic processing and capture its integrity and loading evidence.
fields: lyophiliser ID, loading mode (manual-open / automated / closed barrier) and CCS sterilisation-frequency reference
last SIP cycle ID, end time, result; hold until loading vs APS-challenged maximum; maintenance/cleaning events since SIP
integrity (vent) filter ID, sterilisation record, integrity test result
start-of-cycle leak rate vs specified maximum; chamber leak test frequency status
trays/rings IDs, sterilisation IDs and inspection status
loading pattern (shelf map, trays, vial counts)
transfer method (conveyor, clean-air cart, portable UDAF, closed boxes) and its Grade A status during transfer; transfer start/end
sterile utensil IDs
cycle recipe and key parameters (shelf temperatures, pressures, durations) with alarms
vacuum break gas and its filter
stoppering and stopper seating check at unloading; unseated-stopper handling under Grade A
EM/PM and intervention records for loading/unloading
rules: Manual-open lyophilisers: new successful SIP required before every load (from 25 Aug 2024)
Automated/closed-barrier: SIP interval per CCS enforced
Re-sterilisation required after maintenance or cleaning
Cycle cannot start if leak rate exceeds specified maximum
Vent filter integrity result mandatory for certification
Loading outside the APS-qualified envelope (tray count, loading duration, filtration-to-lyo time, SIP-to-use interval) flagged
Damaged/overdue-inspection trays refused
Sterility samples drawn from each lyophiliser load

name: BB-15 Container closure integrity (CCI) record
purpose: Capture seal-parameter control and integrity testing appropriate to the closure type.
fields: closure type (fusion: glass/plastic ampoule, BFS, FFS, SVP/LVP bag; non-fusion: stopper/crimp, syringe plunger/tip cap)
container volume (<=100 ml or >100 ml)
CCI method (validated; visual inspection not permitted) and equipment ID
100 percent test counts: tested, passed, rejected by reason (fusion <=100 ml)
sampling plan reference and justification (non-fusion or justified reduced sampling >100 ml)
seal parameters (sealing temperatures and uniformity, times, pressures, forming parameters)
vacuum retention test result after predetermined period (vacuum-sealed containers)
mould/tooling ID and change assessment status (BFS/FFS)
rules: Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml require 100 percent CCI; master data cannot select sampling
Visual inspection cannot be selected as CCI method
CCI failure opens investigation and blocks certification
Vacuum-sealed containers: certification blocked until vacuum retention result recorded
Seal parameter excursion segregates units produced in the excursion window

name: BB-16 100 percent visual inspection, acceptance sampling and reject reconciliation
purpose: Document individual inspection of every filled unit, defect classification and a closed unit balance for the batch.
fields: inspection mode (manual / semi-automated / automated)
inspector IDs with VI qualification and eyesight check validity
booth illumination and background check
inspection rate/throughput, continuous inspection time and breaks
AVI recipe and validation reference; challenge-set ID and results at start and at intervals
inspected, accepted, rejected counts by defect code and criticality (critical/major/minor) from controlled defect library
batch-specific alert limits per defect code (from trend data)
post-inspection acceptance sample (e.g. AQL) results by class
unit reconciliation: units filled, removed at interventions, IPC samples, stopper-height rejects, CCI rejects, VI rejects, QC samples, retained samples, APS/other, good units, unexplained difference
rules: Defect rates above product alert limits open an investigation
Any critical defect found in acceptance sampling of accepted units opens an investigation and blocks release (possible 100 percent inspection failure)
Failed AVI interim challenge puts all units since last passing challenge on hold for re-inspection
Reconciliation must close within configured tolerance; unexplained differences block certification
Defect data stored by code for statistical trending and market-impact assessment on adverse trends

name: BB-17 Capping and crimping record
purpose: Document how stoppered vials stay protected until crimped and that displaced stoppers were removed.
fields: capping mode (aseptic with sterilised caps / clean process under Grade A air supply / manual in isolator or Grade A)
cap lot and sterilisation evidence (aseptic mode)
Grade A air supply status at the capper and background grade (>= D)
time from stoppering to crimping
stopper-height detection system qualification status, challenge results, reject count
crimp quality checks (e.g. residual seal force if used)
interventions at capping station
rules: Clean-process capping requires qualified automated stopper-height detection and records its rejects
Loss of Grade A air supply at capping flags affected units
Manual capping only in Grade A locations
Capping rejects included in unit reconciliation

name: BB-18 Bioburden and sterility sampling plan
purpose: Generate and trace worst-case, representative bioburden and sterility samples from execution data.
fields: pre-filtration or pre-terminal-sterilisation bioburden sample: time relative to hold end and filtration/cycle start, location (before first filter if redundant), limit
parametric release: filled-unit bioburden positions and results, organism ID, sterilisation-resistance assessment, endotoxin
sterility samples: start of fill, end of fill, post-critical-intervention samples, cold-spot positions per terminal load (sub-batch), per lyophiliser load
sample origin metadata (unit counter, time, load, position)
LIMS sample IDs and results
short-shelf-life release pathway reference
rules: Bioburden sample must be taken at the worst-case point and before filtration/sterilisation starts
Each terminal-sterilisation load treated as a sub-batch with its own sterility test
Critical interventions add sterility samples per risk rule
Bioburden result against limit and sterility result are release prerequisites unless an approved short-shelf-life or parametric-release pathway applies
Passing sterility test cannot clear open process nonconformances

name: BB-19 Utilities linkage (WFI, pure steam, process gases, cooling/hydraulics)
purpose: Attach the quality state of every high-risk utility used by the batch at the time of use.
fields: point of use (WFI outlet, pure-steam header, gas drop) per step
draw/use time and quantity
WFI loop temperature, flow, TOC, conductivity at use time
daily water sample results for the loop/points used; alert/action status
water system sanitisation events and post-sanitisation chemical / micro / endotoxin result approval status
WFI tank vent filter integrity status
pure steam condensate result and NCG, dryness, superheat test currency
gas lot/CoA or generator status, point-of-use sterilising filter ID and integrity result, periodic gas microbial monitoring status
leak/backflow alarms from hydraulic, heating and cooling systems
rules: Water drawn after a sanitisation is usable only after chemical approval; batches using it are blocked from certification until micro/endotoxin results are approved
Water action excursion links all batches that used the affected point/loop in the relevant period
Steriliser/SIP use flagged if steam quality tests are overdue
Batch-basis gas and vent filter integrity results are release items
Utility alarms in the batch window require assessment

name: BB-20 BFS / FFS process record
purpose: Capture the continuous forming, filling and sealing parameters and integrity controls specific to BFS and FFS.
fields: machine type (BFS shuttle/rotary, FFS single/dual web), background grade
polymer granulate lot / film roll lots with release incl. bioburden/endotoxin
CIP/SIP cycle IDs for product lines and mandrels
extrusion temperature, speed, throat settings; mould temperatures and cooling; forming temperatures/times/pressures; sealing temperatures, uniformity, times, pressures
batch-specific wall-thickness (BFS) and seal strength/uniformity (FFS) test results
fill volume, speed, uniformity checks
printing/embossing/debossing settings
flash-removal cutter settings
parison/support air and product-contact gas filter IDs and integrity status
mould/tooling IDs and change-assessment status
campaign/batch duration timer
interventions requiring stop of extrusion/filling and re-sterilisation
rejects by reason (blowing, forming, sealing, cutting)
100 percent CCI counts
viable EM coverage from assembly to end of filling
rules: Parameter excursions segregate units by time window
Re-sterilisation interventions block resumption until SIP passes
Mould changes without CCI assessment block batch start
Rejects and sealing issues recorded and investigated per threshold
BFS operators in Grade C must be gowned to Grade A/B

name: BB-21 Single-use and closed system verification
purpose: Verify each SUS/closed assembly from receipt to installation and use, including connections.
fields: part number and approved specification/BOM revision
supplier approval status and sterility-assurance verification
lot/serial, sterilisation proof (irradiation certificate, dose range), certificate of conformance
receipt check and pre-use visual check of outer packaging, pouches and labels
opening method and post-installation visual check (holes, kinks, clamps)
E&L/adsorption assessment status for the product; validated maximum contact time
freeze/thaw or transport qualification (where exposed)
connection records: method (intrinsic sterile connector type/lot, SIP after connection, open aseptic in Grade A)
pre-use system integrity (pressure decay) test where required
location grade and integrity-at-every-use evidence when outside Grade A
system opening events with follow-up cleaning/disinfection/sterilisation
rules: Lots without sterilisation proof or from unapproved suppliers stay quarantined
Part number mismatch with BOM refused
Open aseptic connections only in Grade A (or subsequently sterilised)
Closed aseptic systems outside Grade A require an integrity result at every use
Operators performing SUS assembly/connections must be covered by an APS including these manipulations

name: BB-22 Equipment status, alarms and maintenance
purpose: Ensure equipment used is qualified, maintained, released and that its alarms and maintenance events are evaluated against the batch.
fields: equipment ID, sterility-critical flag, qualification status/expiry
preventive maintenance due date and return-to-use approval
unplanned maintenance events with sterility impact assessment
in-cleanroom maintenance with follow-up cleaning, disinfection, extra EM and re-sterilisation tasks
alarm events (critical/non-critical) with acknowledgement, evaluation and time
cleaning status, dirty/clean hold expiry, validated cleaning procedure version
particle counter/probe calibration
rules: Equipment not qualified, overdue for PM or not released after maintenance cannot be used
Critical alarms require immediate documented evaluation before continuation
Unplanned maintenance on sterility-critical equipment requires recorded impact assessment linked to affected batches
In-cleanroom maintenance inserts follow-up tasks that block restart until complete
Equipment sterilisation after reassembly where possible

name: BB-23 Cleanroom cleaning, disinfection and fumigation status
purpose: Keep each room's cleaning/disinfection state current and traceable to validated agents and dilutions.
fields: room/zone, date/time, cleaning performed (before disinfection)
disinfectant/detergent, lot, sterile status (Grade A/B), expiry
dilution preparation record: time, container status, in-use expiry, microbial monitoring result
rotation of agents with different modes of action; sporicide application date and due date
residue removal cleaning
fumigation/VHP cycle ID and outcome
operator and verifier
rules: Grade A/B only sterile disinfectants/detergents (C/D where CCS requires)
Expired dilutions rejected
Disinfection without preceding cleaning flagged
Overdue cleaning or sporicide sets room 'not ready' and blocks steps
Failed fumigation keeps the room unavailable

name: BB-24 QA review and QP certification package (Annex 1 view)
purpose: Present every Annex 1-required element for the batch in one place and prevent certification until all are complete, reviewed and acceptable.
fields: batch header: product, sterility route (terminal / aseptic / aseptic + post-aseptic heat treatment), parametric-release and short-shelf-life flags, CCS version
review-by-exception list: deviations, non-qualified interventions, alarms, hold-time exceedances, parameter excursions, supervised entries, QA exceptions
all sterilisation cycle IDs contributing to the batch with conformity approval
filter test results (PUPSIT or waiver ref, post-use, redundant logic outcome, gas and vent filters, lyophiliser integrity filter)
EM/PM results and trends for all rooms/zones and the whole processing window; pending samples
utility status (water results incl. post-sanitisation approvals, steam, gases)
APS status of the line/process/shift and of each participating operator at time of manufacture
personnel qualification snapshot for all signers
lyophiliser leak rate and SIP status
CCI results, vacuum retention (if applicable), 100 percent inspection results, AQL, reconciliation
bioburden results and sterility results (per sub-batch/load)
linked investigations with batch-scope rationale and status
QP/QA reviewer identity and sterile-manufacturing competence
rules: Certification hard-blocked while any linked investigation is open
Certification blocked if any sterilisation cycle, filter test or vent/gas filter result is missing, failed or unapproved
Certification blocked while EM/PM samples in the processing window are pending, unless an approved short-shelf-life pathway applies (then most recent data reviewed)
Certification blocked while water micro/endotoxin post-sanitisation results for water used are unapproved
Certification blocked if the line APS was failed/suspended at time of manufacture or an APS failure investigation includes the batch
Sterility test pass cannot override any open process nonconformance
EM/trend review signature required

name: BB-25 Master batch record configuration validator (Injectables edition)
purpose: Stop non-compliant recipes at design time so execution-time checks have correct inputs.
fields: product sterility route and justification reference (terminal preferred; aseptic; aseptic + post-aseptic heat treatment)
dosage form and risk flags (supports growth, long hold, non-filterable, ointment/suspension/emulsion, hazardous material, manual aseptic, short shelf life, parametric release)
container/closure type and volume (drives CCI rule), vacuum-sealed flag
per-step required grade and zone type, step type (aseptic / clean / non-classified), CCS critical control point tag and reference
filter train definition and MA-registered filter
validated time windows and limits (with validation references)
intervention catalogue binding and unit-removal numbers
EM programme binding
sterilisation cycles/load patterns referenced
CCS impact assessment for each change
rules: Reject limits looser than Annex 1 minimums (particle and viable tables, requalification and APS intervals) without documented QA justification
Aseptic set-up, connections, filling, lyo loading and open-container transfers must be Grade A steps with qualified background
TS preparation at least Grade D (C when risk flags set); TS filling at least Grade C (A in C when unusual risk)
Fusion-sealed containers up to 100 ml must carry 100 percent CCI; visual inspection not a CCI method; UV not a sterilisation method
Non-filterable products require sterile additions and sterile contact equipment
Master record changes require CCS impact assessment before approval and effectiveness check after

name: BB-26 Terminal sterilisation of filled product (loads as sub-batches)
purpose: Map filled units to steriliser loads and prove each load achieved the validated lethality without damaging containers.
fields: prep-to-fill and fill-to-sterilisation times vs limits
pre-sterilisation bioburden sample (worst case, end of hold) and result
load ID = sub-batch ID, units per load, load pattern, validated reference
cycle data: F0 / temperature-time, equilibration, probe positions correlated to worst-case (slowest heating) positions
superheated-water checks (nozzles, drains) and cooling-water sterility evidence
non-rigid container deformation/leak inspection after cycle
sterility samples from cold-spot positions of each load
parametric release flag and critical-parameter review
post-aseptic terminal heat treatment flag (where used)
rules: Units from a failed or deviating load cannot be released and are segregated by load
Each load tested for sterility separately (unless parametric release authorised)
Filled units not sterilised within the time limit trigger deviation
Deformed/leaking non-rigid containers recorded as rejects in reconciliation

requirement: Contamination controls for microbial, endotoxin/pyrogen and particle sources are interrelated; although usually assessed, controlled and monitored one by one, their combined effectiveness should be judged together.
system_implications: Besides per-record checks, the batch review must offer a consolidated contamination-control view (timeline overlaying interventions, EM/particle data, DP/air alarms, hold times, sterilisation and filter results, personnel events) so reviewers judge the batch as a whole rather than as isolated passes.
verification_test: Open the batch timeline; confirm interventions, particle spikes, EM positives and alarms are displayed on one time axis and exportable.

requirement: Sterile manufacture takes place in cleanrooms entered via change rooms acting as personnel airlocks and via material airlocks, supplied with suitably filtered air and kept to the right cleanliness standard; scientifically justified controls and monitoring evaluate the state of cleanrooms, airlocks and pass-through hatches.
system_implications: The batch's EM scope must include the airlocks, change rooms and pass-through hatches actually used for personnel and material entry (derived from gowning and transfer records), not only the processing rooms.
verification_test: Transfer material through pass-through PT-2 during the batch; confirm PT-2 monitoring data appear in the batch EM summary.

requirement: Cleaning ahead of barrier-system bio-decontamination is declared essential, because leftover residues can defeat the decontamination.
system_implications: Hard sequence rule: an isolator/RABS bio-decontamination cycle is accepted as valid for the batch only if a completed cleaning record for the same enclosure precedes it with no intervening use.
verification_test: Record a VHP cycle with no prior cleaning record; confirm the cycle is marked invalid for batch use.

requirement: Visual inspection is declared not acceptable as a container-closure integrity test method.
system_implications: The CCI method list excludes visual inspection; a 100 percent visual inspection record can never satisfy a CCI requirement in master data or at release.
verification_test: Attempt to map the 100 percent visual inspection step as the CCI evidence for an ampoule product; confirm refusal.

requirement: For closed systems in aseptic processing, keeping every product-contact surface sterile is declared critical.
system_implications: Every product-contact element of an aseptic closed system (bags, tubing, connectors, sensors, filters) must resolve to a sterilisation record or supplier sterility proof before the system is released for use; no element may be 'not applicable'.
verification_test: Build a closed assembly where one connector has no sterility evidence; confirm the assembly cannot be released for use.

requirement: A passing sterility test is declared incapable of assuring sterility for a product that did not meet its design, procedural or validation parameters.
system_implications: Release logic hard rule: sterility-test results are evaluated only after all process, procedural and validation-status checks pass; a pass never closes or overrides an open nonconformance.
verification_test: Enter a passing sterility result for a batch with an unresolved sterilisation-cycle deviation; confirm status remains 'not releasable'.
